definition_zh: 大型客机；班机；（行业用法）客机这一类别
definition_en: a large aircraft built to carry fare-paying passengers on scheduled routes; also the class of such aircraft or the business of operating them
core_image: 一条固定航线上的大班机
scene: 这架宽体机每天往返两地，客座率一直很高。 The airliner carries three hundred passengers.
sceneCN: 这里 airliner 是「大型客机」（第 1 个义项：按固定航线载客的大型飞机）；句意为这架客机载客三百人。核心画面是一条固定航线上的大班机。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -er 的部分，义为「航空公司；航线」
去掉 air- 的部分，义为「班轮；定期客轮」
air 加 lift，义为「空运；空中补给」

senses.title: A large passenger aircraft
senses.definition: a big aircraft built to carry fare-paying passengers on scheduled routes, as opposed to a cargo or private plane
senses.definitionCN: 为在固定航线上运送付费旅客而造的大型飞机，与货机或私人飞机相对
senses.example: The airliner turned back after an engine warning.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机报警后，这架客机返航了。
senses.why: Liner once meant a ship running a fixed line, so airliner simply moves that idea into the sky: a ship of the air on a set route.
senses.whyCN: liner 原指跑固定航线的船，所以 airliner 只是把这个想法搬到天上：一条固定航线上的空中班轮。

senses.title: The class of aircraft as a trade
senses.definition: the class of aircraft or the business of running them, used collectively in industry and news writing
senses.definitionCN: 这一类飞机或经营它们的业务，在行业与新闻文本中作集合用法
senses.example: Airliner orders fell sharply that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年客机订单大幅下滑。
senses.why: Here the word stops pointing at one machine and names the whole category, the same shift that happens with aircraft and tonnage.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词不再指一架机器，而是指整个类别，与 aircraft、tonnage 的用法变化相同。

intro.en: Airliner is a sea word lifted into the sky: line gave liner, a ship on a fixed route, and air turned that ship into an aircraft.
intro.cn: airliner 是一个被抬到天上的航海词：line 派生出 liner「跑固定航线的船」，air 再把这条船变成飞机。

items.en: Latin linea meant a linen thread and then a straight line, from linum, flax.
items.cn: 拉丁语 linea 先指亚麻线，后指直线，源自 linum「亚麻」。

items.en: Old French ligne kept the sense of a line or route, and English took it as line.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 保留「线、路线」之义，英语借作 line。

items.en: By the nineteenth century a liner was a ship sailing a published line of ports, not a wandering trader.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，liner 指按公布航线挂靠港口的大船，而不是四处揽货的散船。

items.en: English added air to line for routes flown on a schedule, first used in the nineteen twenties.
items.cn: 英语把 air 加到 line 上，表示按时刻表飞行的航线，最早用于二十世纪二十年代。

items.en: Adding -er to airline produced airliner, the aircraft that flies the line, modelled directly on the steamship liner.
items.cn: 在 airline 上加 -er 得到 airliner，即飞这条航线的飞机，直接仿照蒸汽班轮 liner 构词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the air- and liner compounds; the near-meaning group lists other words for a passenger-carrying plane.
note.cn: 形近组保留 air- 与 liner 复合词；近义组列出其他表示「载客飞机」的词。

entries.definition: A company operating scheduled air services.
entries.definitionCN: 经营定期航空运输的公司。

entries.definition: A large ship sailing a fixed route.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定航线航行的大船。

entries.definition: Ground where aircraft take off and land.
entries.definitionCN: 供飞机起降的场地。

entries.definition: The main performer on a bill.
entries.definitionCN: 演出单上的主角。

entries.definition: A large airliner powered by jet engines.
entries.definitionCN: 由喷气发动机驱动的大型客机。

entries.definition: Any machine capable of flight.
entries.definitionCN: 任何能飞行的机器。

entries.definition: A very large jet, informally a jumbo jet.
entries.definitionCN: 特大型喷气客机，口语称大型珍宝机。

entries.definition: An aircraft, the everyday short form.
entries.definitionCN: 飞机，日常简称。

normalIntro.en: Airliner is airline plus -er: the machine that flies the line of an airline.
normalIntro.cn: airliner 就是 airline 加 -er：飞航空公司那条航线的机器。

normal.en: A liner was first a ship, so an airliner is a ship of the air.
normal.cn: liner 最早是船，所以 airliner 就是空中的船。

normal.en: -er here marks the thing that does the job, as in tanker and freighter.
normal.cn: 这里的 -er 表示干这活的东西，如 tanker、freighter。

normal.en: Airline is the company; airliner is the plane. Never swap them.
normal.cn: airline 是公司，airliner 是飞机，两者绝不能互换。

normal.en: It is countable, so say four wide-body airliners.
normal.cn: 它可数，所以说 four wide-body airliners。

normal.en: Airliners carry passengers; freighters carry cargo.
normal.cn: airliner 载客，freighter 载货。

abstract.en: Picture an ocean liner with wings instead of a hull.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘远洋班轮，船体换成了机翼。

abstract.en: Imagine a bus route drawn across the sky with a timetable.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画在天空中的公交线，还配着时刻表。

abstract.en: Think of a ship that docks at gates instead of ports.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船，停靠的不是港口而是登机口。

examples.en: The airliner taxied slowly through the rain.
examples.cn: 客机在雨中缓缓滑行。

examples.en: Two airliners were grounded by the storm.
examples.cn: 两架客机因暴风雨停飞。

examples.en: The new airliner burns less fuel per seat.
examples.cn: 这款新客机每个座位的油耗更低。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「艾尔莱纳」——艾尔（air）是天，莱纳（liner）是班轮：天上的班轮，就是大型客机。

root: 拉丁语 linea「亚麻线、直线」经古法语 ligne 进入英语成为 line，加 -er 构成 liner「按固定航线航行的大船」；二十世纪把 air 与 line 拼合成 airline，再加 -er 得到 airliner，字面即「飞固定航线的空中班轮」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from the shipping idea of a fixed line: one names the aircraft that flies it, the other names the whole class of such aircraft.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都来自航运里「固定航线」的想法：一个指飞这条航线的飞机，一个指这一整类飞机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ocean liner moved into the sky
core.cn: 核心意象：一艘搬到天上的远洋班轮

branches.en: A wide-body jet on a daily route.
branches.cn: 每天飞固定航线的宽体喷气机。

branches.en: Rows of fare-paying seats.
branches.cn: 一排排付费旅客的座位。

branches.en: Manufacturers counting annual orders.
branches.cn: 制造商统计年度订单。

branches.en: A fleet retired after twenty years.
branches.cn: 一批用了二十年后退役的机队。

branches.en: Both keep the idea of a fixed line.
branches.cn: 两者都保留「固定航线」的想法。

intro.en: Airliner is layered: air names the medium, line names the route, and -er names the vehicle that serves it.
intro.cn: airliner 是分层的：air 指媒介，line 指航线，-er 指跑这条航线的载具。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea, from linum, flax, gave line and liner; the air half and the final -er are English additions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linea 源自 linum「亚麻」，产生 line 与 liner；air 这一半与最后的 -er 是英语后加的。

latinEntries.example: Linum is the plant behind line.
latinEntries.exampleCN: linum 是 line 背后的植物。

definition_zh: 持续进行的；仍在进行中的；尚未结束的；不断发生的
definition_en: still happening or continuing, and not yet finished or settled
core_image: 一个人沿着同一条路一直往前走，脚下不停
scene: 这里指「持续进行的」。 An ongoing investigation kept the office busy through the winter.
sceneCN: 这里 ongoing 是「仍在进行、尚未结束」（第 2 个义项：进行中的调查）；句意：一项仍在进行的调查让办公室忙了一整个冬天。图中可辨识物件：堆满文件的办公桌、墙上的案件时间线、亮着的台灯、写着“未结案”的标签。

pos.zh: 持续进行的；进行中的；尚未结束的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 行走；离去；进行中的（go 的动名词与现在分词）
（常指可疑的）活动；发生的事情

senses.title: Still going: continuing without a stop
senses.definition: continuing to happen or develop, without having stopped
senses.definitionCN: 继续发生或发展，并没有停下来
senses.example: The river is an ongoing source of power for the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河一直是村子持续不断的动力来源。
senses.why: Ongoing is simply on 'continuing' plus going 'walking'. The picture is someone still on the road, one step after another, with no arrival and no halt.
senses.whyCN: ongoing 就是 on“继续”加 going“走”。画面是一个人仍在路上，一步一步，既没有到达，也没有停歇。

senses.title: In progress now: an ongoing investigation
senses.titleCN: 进行中：此刻仍在办的调查
senses.definition: currently being carried out, used of work that has started and is not yet over
senses.definitionCN: 目前正在被执行，用于已经开始而尚未结束的工作
senses.example: An ongoing investigation kept the office busy through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 一项仍在进行的调查让办公室忙了一整个冬天。
senses.why: The walking is happening at this moment. English uses ongoing for official work precisely because the result is not in yet: the case is still on the road.
senses.whyCN: “走”正发生在此刻。英语用 ongoing 形容公务，正因为结果还没出来：案子还在路上。

senses.title: Not yet finished: an ongoing project
senses.titleCN: 尚未完成：还在做的项目
senses.definition: not completed, used of a task, building or piece of work still under way
senses.definitionCN: 尚未完成，用于仍在施工或推进的任务、工程
senses.example: The ongoing bridge repairs will last until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 仍在进行的桥梁维修会持续到春天。
senses.why: If the walk has not ended, the destination has not been reached. Not finishing is the negative face of the same continuing motion.
senses.whyCN: 如果行走没有结束，终点就还没到达。“未完成”是同一段持续运动的否定面。

senses.title: Continuing over a long period: ongoing support
senses.definition: continuing for a long time, often of help, care or relationships
senses.definitionCN: 长时间持续，常用于帮助、照护或关系
senses.example: The charity offers ongoing support to families after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪灾过后，这家慈善机构为家庭提供持续支持。
senses.why: Here the road is long and the walking steady: help that does not stop after the first emergency but keeps pace with the family.
senses.whyCN: 这里路很长，脚步很稳：帮助不是应急一次就结束，而是与这个家庭同步走下去。

senses.title: Recurring regularly: ongoing costs
senses.definition: recurring again and again rather than happening once, used of costs, duties and maintenance
senses.definitionCN: 一次又一次地反复出现而非只发生一次，用于费用、职责与维护
senses.example: Ongoing costs include rent, insurance and repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 持续费用包括房租、保险和维修。
senses.why: A single payment ends; a cost that keeps coming is a walk that keeps returning to the same stretch of road, so the adjective marks repetition as well as duration.
senses.whyCN: 一次性付款会结束；不断出现的费用则像总回到同一段路上的行走，因此这个形容词既标持续时间，也标反复。

senses.title: Gradual and continuing: ongoing decline
senses.titleCN: 逐步而持续：不断加剧的衰退
senses.definition: continuing steadily in one direction, used of changes that develop over time
senses.definitionCN: 朝一个方向稳定持续，用于随时间发展的变化
senses.example: The ongoing decline in rainfall worries local farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 降雨量持续下降让当地农民担忧。
senses.why: A slow change is still motion: the walk continues in the same direction, and the lack of a stop is what makes the trend serious.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢的变化仍是运动：行走朝同一方向继续，而“不停”正是这种趋势令人担忧的原因。

senses.title: Medical: a condition still present
senses.titleCN: 医学用法：症状仍然存在
senses.definition: still present after treatment or over time, used of symptoms and conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在治疗后或经过一段时间仍然存在，用于症状与病情
senses.example: Patients reported ongoing pain six months after the surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 患者表示术后六个月仍有持续疼痛。
senses.why: In medicine the walk is the symptom's course: it has not stopped, so the condition is not resolved and must still be managed.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，行走就是症状的病程：它没有停下，所以病情未解除，仍需处理。

senses.title: A process with no clear end point
senses.definition: used of processes that have no natural finish and simply keep developing
senses.definitionCN: 用于没有天然终点、只是一直发展下去的过程
senses.example: Language change is an ongoing process, not a project with a deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 语言变化是一个持续的过程，不是有截止日期的项目。
senses.why: Some roads have no gate at the end. When a process cannot be completed by definition, ongoing names its permanent condition rather than a temporary stage.
senses.whyCN: 有些路尽头没有门。当一个过程按定义就无法完成时，ongoing 命名的是它的永久状态，而不是某个临时阶段。

senses.title: Unresolved: an ongoing debate
senses.titleCN: 未有定论：仍在争的辩论
senses.definition: still being argued or decided, used of disputes and questions without a settled answer
senses.definitionCN: 仍在争论或决定中，用于没有定论的争议与问题
senses.example: Whether to build the dam remains an ongoing debate.
senses.exampleCN: 是否修建大坝仍是一场未有定论的争论。
senses.why: The walking here is argument going back and forth. Because no side has stopped, the question is still open and the debate is ongoing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的行走是来回往复的争论。因为没有一方停下，问题仍未闭合，辩论便处于 ongoing 状态。

intro.en: Ongoing is a modern English compound recorded from 1877: on 'continuing' plus going 'walking'. It is not a classical root word, and no Latin ancestry should be invented for it.
intro.cn: ongoing 是 1877 年有记录的现代英语复合词：on“继续”加 going“走”。它不是古典词根词，不应为它编造拉丁来源。

items.en: Ongoing is first recorded in 1877 as an adjective meaning 'continuing, still in progress'.
items.cn: ongoing 于 1877 年首次被记录为形容词，意为“继续的、仍在进行的”。

items.en: The word is on 'on, onward' plus going, the present participle of go: literally 'going on'.
items.cn: 这个词由 on“继续、向前”加 going（go 的现在分词）构成，字面就是“一直走着”。

items.en: Going is a gerund formed around 1300 from go. Old English had no such form; its inherited noun for a journey was gang.
items.cn: going 是约 1300 年由 go 构成的动名词。古英语没有这个形式，它固有的表示“行程”的名词是 gang。

items.en: The verb go continues Old English gān 'to go, walk'; its past went comes from a different verb, wendan 'to turn, go'.
items.cn: 动词 go 继承古英语 gān“走、行走”；它的过去式 went 来自另一个动词 wendan“转、去”。

items.en: In the 20th century ongoing spreads into administration, finance, medicine and journalism: ongoing investigation, ongoing costs, ongoing symptoms.
items.cn: 20 世纪，ongoing 扩展到行政、金融、医学与新闻语言：ongoing investigation、ongoing costs、ongoing symptoms。

items.en: Both ongoing and the hyphenated on-going are used today; the solid spelling is now standard in most styles.
items.cn: 今天 ongoing 与带连字符的 on-going 两种写法都在用；多数体例以连写为标准。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: coming toward you, as of traffic. It shares on- but means approaching, not continuing.
entries.definitionCN: 迎面而来的，如车流。它同样以 on- 开头，但意思是“接近”，不是“持续”。

entries.definition: friendly and sociable, or leaving a place. It joins out- to going and has nothing to do with continuation.
entries.definitionCN: 外向友善的；离去的。它把 out- 加在 going 上，与“持续”无关。

entries.definition: the act of leaving, or the condition of travel. It is the participle on which ongoing is built.
entries.definitionCN: 离开；行走状况。它是构成 ongoing 的分词本身。

entries.definition: going on without any interruption. It is stricter than ongoing, which allows pauses and repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无中断地进行。它比 ongoing 更严格，后者允许停顿与反复。

entries.definition: still carrying on after a start. It is close to ongoing but sounds more like a description of an action than a label.
entries.definitionCN: 开始之后仍在继续。它与 ongoing 接近，但更像描述动作，而非贴标签。

entries.definition: not completed. It states the missing end, while ongoing states the continuing motion.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未完成。它说的是缺少结尾，ongoing 说的是持续的运动。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: on plus going, the verb go and its participle, and the fixed phrases ongoing investigation and ongoing costs.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：on + going、动词 go 及其分词，以及固定搭配 ongoing investigation、ongoing costs。

normal.en: on 'onward' plus going 'walking' gives 'walking on': the person has not stopped and has not arrived.
normal.cn: on“向前”加 going“走”就是“一直走”：人既没停，也没到。

normal.en: Going is the present participle of go, so ongoing is built from an everyday verb rather than a Latin root.
normal.cn: going 是 go 的现在分词，因此 ongoing 是由日常动词构成，而非拉丁词根。

normal.en: Old English gang also meant 'a going, journey'; going replaced it as the ordinary noun.
normal.cn: 古英语 gang 也指“行走、旅程”；going 后来取代它成为普通名词。

normal.en: An ongoing investigation is a case still on the road, with no result yet.
normal.cn: an ongoing investigation 是仍在路上的案子，结果还没出来。

normal.en: Ongoing costs are payments that keep returning, like a walk that keeps coming back to the same stretch.
normal.cn: ongoing costs 是不断回来的支出，像总回到同一段路上的行走。

abstract.en: Picture a walker on a road with no gate in sight: the only fact about him is that he is still walking.
abstract.cn: 想象一个行者走在望不见门的路上：关于他的唯一事实就是还在走。

abstract.en: The walk can be a case, a bridge, a decline, a pain, or an argument; what they share is that the motion has not stopped.
abstract.cn: 这段行走可以是一桩案子、一座桥、一场衰退、一处疼痛或一场争论；共同点是运动没有停止。

abstract.en: When the road has no end by nature, ongoing stops describing a stage and names a permanent condition.
abstract.cn: 当路本身就没有尽头，ongoing 便不再描述某个阶段，而是在命名一种永久状态。

examples.en: The archive is an ongoing project that will take another decade.
examples.cn: 这项档案工程仍在进行，还要再花十年。

examples.en: Ongoing repairs have closed one lane of the bridge since March.
examples.cn: 自三月起，持续进行的维修封住了桥的一条车道。

examples.en: Their ongoing disagreement about the budget delayed the vote.
examples.cn: 他们在预算上持续不断的分歧推迟了表决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂，够硬」——昂，够硬！这工程一直在进行，从来没停过 → ongoing 持续进行的

root: 现代英语复合词 on“继续、向前”+ going“走”（go 的现在分词，go 继承古英语 gān“行走”），1877 年始见记录；与古典词根无关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of ongoing all start from one picture: a walker still on the road. The same continuing motion then covers official work, unfinished projects, long-term help, recurring costs, slow trends, symptoms, endless processes and open arguments.
sensesIntro.cn: ongoing 的九个义项都从同一幅画出发：一个行者仍在路上。同一段持续运动随后覆盖公务、未完成的工程、长期帮助、反复费用、缓慢趋势、症状、无尽过程与未有定论的争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker still moving along the same road, with no stop and no arrival.
core.cn: 核心意象：行者沿着同一条路继续走，既没有停，也没有到。

branches.en: THE WALK ITSELF: motion that continues, including processes that have no end point at all.
branches.cn: 行走本身：持续不断的运动，也包括根本没有终点的过程。

branches.en: WORK UNDER WAY: an investigation or a project that has started and has not finished.
branches.cn: 在办之事：已经启动而尚未结束的调查或工程。

branches.en: THE LONG ROAD: help that keeps pace over years, and costs that keep returning.
branches.cn: 长路：经年同步的支持，以及不断回来的费用。

branches.en: THE STEADY COURSE: a trend that keeps moving one way, and a symptom that has not stopped.
branches.cn: 稳定的走向：一直朝一个方向推进的趋势，以及没有停下的症状。

branches.en: THE OPEN QUESTION: a debate still going back and forth with no settled answer.
branches.cn: 未决之问：仍在来回、没有定论的辩论。

intro.en: Ongoing is a native English compound of on plus the present participle going, with no Latin prefix. English adds -ly and -ness to it, and the same going also appears in outgoing and easygoing.
intro.cn: ongoing 是英语本土复合词，由 on 加现在分词 going 构成，没有拉丁前缀。英语又给它加 -ly、-ness，同一个 going 也出现在 outgoing、easygoing 中。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for ongoing. Its oldest forms are Germanic: Old English gān 'to go' and the noun gang 'a going, journey'. The entries below give those forms rather than Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: ongoing 没有拉丁语来源。它最早的形式属于日耳曼语：古英语 gān“走”和名词 gang“行走、旅程”。下面给出这些形式，而不是拉丁词。

items.structure: on- (on, onward) + going (present participle of go)
items.meaning: still going on; continuing and not finished
items.meaningCN: 仍在进行的；持续的；未结束的
items.example: The cleanup is ongoing after the storm.
items.exampleCN: 风暴过后的清理仍在进行。

items.meaningCN: 持续地；不间断地（罕用，-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The team meets ongoingly to review the case.
items.exampleCN: 团队持续开会复审此案。

items.meaningCN: 持续性；进行状态（罕用，-ness 构成名词）
items.example: The ongoingness of the war exhausted both sides.
items.exampleCN: 战争的持续不断让双方都筋疲力尽。

items.meaning: the act of leaving or travelling; that which goes
items.meaningCN: 离开；行走；进行中的（go 的动名词与分词）
items.example: The going was slow on the wet track.
items.exampleCN: 在湿滑的小路上走得很慢。

items.meaning: events or activities, often suspicious ones
items.meaningCN: 发生的活动；（常指可疑的）勾当
items.example: She wanted to know about the goings-on next door.
items.exampleCN: 她想知道隔壁在搞什么名堂。

items.meaningCN: 外向的；离去的（out-“向外”+ going）
items.example: He is the most outgoing member of the team.
items.exampleCN: 他是队里最外向的成员。

items.example: Her easygoing manner calms the whole office.
items.exampleCN: 她随和的态度让整个办公室都安定下来。

items.meaning: to experience or pass through something
items.meaningCN: 经历；经受（under- + go“走”，即从下面走过）
items.example: The building will undergo major repairs.

items.structure: go (bare verb from Old English gān)
items.meaning: to move from one place to another
items.example: They go to the market every Saturday.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 行走；旅程；通道；进程（古英语）

definition_zh: 坟墓；陵墓；墓室；葬身之处
definition_en: a grave or a built structure that holds a dead body, especially one made of stone and intended to be permanent
core_image: 一座石砌墓室嵌在山坡里，门楣上刻着名字，门内一片黑暗，外面是明亮的沙地
scene: 山坡上凿出一座石砌墓室，门楣刻着名字，门内一片黑暗，外面是明亮的沙地。 Cut into the hillside, the tomb keeps its carved name above a door that opens into darkness.
sceneCN: 这里 tomb 指「容纳遗体的石造墓室或坟墓」（第 1 个义项：以构筑物形式保存遗体的墓葬）；句意为山坡里凿出的墓室门楣上刻着名字，门内昏暗，门外是明亮沙地。可辨识物件：石墓门、门楣刻字、黑暗墓室、沙地、台阶。

senses.title: A grave, especially a built one
senses.definition: a place where a dead body is laid, typically a stone structure rather than a simple pit
senses.definitionCN: 安放遗体的地方，通常是有石造构筑的墓而非简单土坑
senses.example: The tomb was cut directly into the rock.
senses.exampleCN: 这座墓直接凿进岩石中。
senses.why: Tomb goes back through Latin tumba to Greek tymbos, a burial mound; the word began as a heap over a grave and then named the structure itself.
senses.whyCN: tomb 经拉丁 tumba 上溯希腊 tymbos「坟丘」；这个词起初指盖在墓上的土堆，后来指构筑本身。

senses.title: A grand monumental tomb
senses.titleCN: 陵墓：宏大纪念性的墓葬建筑
senses.definition: a large, often royal or public monument built to hold and honour the dead
senses.definitionCN: 为容纳并纪念死者而建的大型、常为王室或公共的纪念建筑
senses.example: The royal tomb took thirty years to build.
senses.exampleCN: 这座王陵修了三十年。
senses.why: Scale turns a grave into a monument; the word then carries architecture, ceremony and public memory at once.
senses.whyCN: 规模把坟墓变成纪念物；这个词于是同时承载建筑、仪式与公共记忆。

senses.title: The chamber inside
senses.titleCN: 墓室：容纳遗体的内部空间
senses.definition: the inner room of a tomb where the body and goods are placed
senses.definitionCN: 墓中安放遗体与随葬品的内部空间
senses.example: The tomb chamber was painted with scenes of the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 墓室内壁绘有收获场景。
senses.why: A tomb is both shell and room, and the word shifts between the outside structure and the inside space.
senses.whyCN: 墓既是外壳也是房间，这个词在外部构筑与内部空间之间转换。

senses.title: A stone container for the dead
senses.titleCN: 石椁：包住遗体的石制容器
senses.definition: a stone coffin or enclosure that holds a body or a coffin
senses.definitionCN: 容纳遗体或棺材的石制棺椁或围护
senses.example: The body lay inside a tomb of cut stone.
senses.exampleCN: 遗体安放在一座凿石椁中。
senses.why: The boundary between a room and a container is thin: once the structure is small and closed, tomb names the box.
senses.whyCN: 房间与容器的界线很薄：一旦构筑变小并封闭，tomb 就指那只石箱。

senses.title: An archaeological tomb unit
senses.titleCN: 考古墓葬单位：作为记录对象的墓
senses.definition: a tomb recorded as one structure with its contents and construction history
senses.definitionCN: 连同内容与建造过程作为一个整体记录的墓葬构筑
senses.example: The tomb was recorded as a single unit with its shaft.
senses.exampleCN: 这座墓连同竖井被作为一个单位记录。
senses.why: Excavators need stable units, so the whole built grave, shaft and chamber become one tomb on the plan.
senses.whyCN: 发掘者需要稳定的单位，于是整座构筑墓、竖井与墓室在平面图上成为一座 tomb。

senses.title: A holy tomb
senses.titleCN: 圣陵：宗教传统中的圣者之墓
senses.definition: the tomb of a saint or prophet, often a place of pilgrimage
senses.definitionCN: 圣徒或先知之墓，常为朝圣之地
senses.example: Pilgrims came to the holy tomb for healing.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者来到这座圣陵求医治。
senses.why: A holy person's tomb becomes a contact point between the living and the sacred, so the structure gains a devotional role.
senses.whyCN: 圣者之墓成为生者与神圣之间的接触点，这座构筑于是获得敬礼功能。

senses.title: A single chamber in a catacomb
senses.definition: one excavated room within a network of underground galleries used for burials
senses.definitionCN: 地下墓道网络中用于埋葬的一个开凿室
senses.example: Each family tomb in the catacomb has its own niche.
senses.exampleCN: 地下墓穴中每个家族墓室都有自己的壁龛。
senses.why: Underground burial multiplies small rooms, and each room is a tomb in the countable sense.
senses.whyCN: 地下埋葬造出许多小室，每个小室都是可数意义上的 tomb。

senses.title: A place of death, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻：葬身之处或死亡之地
senses.definition: used figuratively for a place or situation that ends a life, a career or a hope
senses.definitionCN: 比喻终结生命、事业或希望的地方或处境
senses.example: The valley was a tomb for the expedition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个谷地成了探险队的葬身之处。
senses.why: If a tomb is where something is finally laid to rest, then any fatal or final place can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 如果墓是某物最终安息之处，那么任何致命或终结性的地方都能借用这个名字。

intro.en: Tomb came into English through Old French tombe from Latin tumba, itself borrowed from Greek tymbos, a burial mound. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tomb 经古法语 tombe 来自拉丁 tumba，而 tumba 又借自希腊 tymbos「坟丘」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tymbos meant a burial mound or a grave, and it is related to a Greek verb meaning to swell, because a mound is heaped up.
items.cn: tymbos 意为坟丘或坟墓，与一个意为「鼓起」的希腊动词相关，因为坟丘是堆起来的。

items.en: Latin borrowed tymbos as tumba, keeping the sense of a grave and extending it to the built structure.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 tymbos 为 tumba，保留坟墓义，并扩展到构筑物。

items.en: Old French tombe carried the word into English after the Norman conquest, first as a grave and then as a monument.
items.cn: 古法语 tombe 在诺曼征服后把词带入英语，最初指墓，后指纪念性墓葬。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word increasingly named large built tombs, while grave remained the plain term for a dug pit.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，这个词越来越多指大型构筑墓，而 grave 仍是普通土坑的常用词。

items.en: Source uncertain: the link between tymbos and the swelling verb is generally accepted but not certain, and the exact route through Old French dialects is not fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：tymbos 与「鼓起」动词的联系一般被接受，但并非确证；经古法语各方言的具体路径也缺乏完整记载。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close to tomb; the second group holds words for graves and monuments.
note.cn: 第一组是形音上与 tomb 接近的词；第二组是坟墓与纪念性建筑的词。

entries.definition: The stone that marks a tomb; the tomb is the grave or structure beneath or behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 标记墓葬的石块；tomb 是它下方或后方的墓与构筑。

entries.definition: To place in a tomb or to serve as a tomb for something; it is the action, not the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 放入墓中，或作为某物的墓；它是动作，不是构筑。

entries.definition: A burial mound, from the same Latin stock; it names the heap rather than the chamber.
entries.definitionCN: 坟丘，同出拉丁词干；它指土堆，而非墓室。

entries.definition: A dug place for a body; tomb usually implies a built or marked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为遗体挖的坑；tomb 通常暗示有构筑或标记。

entries.definition: A large monumental building containing tombs; it is the house, while a tomb can be a single chamber.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳墓葬的大型纪念建筑；它是房屋，而 tomb 可以是单个墓室。

entries.definition: An underground vault beneath a church used for burials; it is a room within a larger building.
entries.definitionCN: 教堂下用于埋葬的地下室；它是更大建筑中的一个房间。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek mound, the Latin borrowing, the royal monument and the chamber inside.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊坟丘、拉丁借词、王陵纪念建筑，以及内部墓室。

normal.en: tymbos, a mound, became Latin tumba and English tomb: the word starts as a heap over a grave.
normal.cn: tymbos「坟丘」变成拉丁 tumba 与英语 tomb：这个词起初是盖在墓上的土堆。

normal.en: A tomb can be the structure outside or the chamber inside.
normal.cn: tomb 既可以指外部构筑，也可以指内部墓室。

normal.en: Scale turns a grave into a monument, and the word then carries public memory.
normal.cn: 规模把坟墓变成纪念物，这个词于是承载公共记忆。

normal.en: A saint's tomb becomes a pilgrimage destination.
normal.cn: 圣者之墓会成为朝圣地。

normal.en: In metaphor, any fatal place can be called a tomb.
normal.cn: 在比喻中，任何致命之地都能被称为 tomb。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a tomb is architecture built around a single fact: someone is not coming back.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，tomb 是围绕一个事实建造的建筑：有人不会再回来。

abstract.en: The word holds both container and room, both body and memory.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时容纳容器与房间、身体与记忆。

abstract.en: Every monument to the dead is also a claim by the living about status.
abstract.cn: 每一座死者纪念物，也是生者关于身份的一次主张。

examples.en: The tomb was sealed with a single massive stone.
examples.cn: 这座墓被一块巨大的石头封住。

examples.en: Paintings inside the tomb show the dead man hunting.
examples.cn: 墓内壁画描绘墓主狩猎的场景。

examples.en: The valley proved a tomb for the lost expedition.
examples.cn: 这个谷地成了失踪探险队的葬身之处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tomb」读音近「土墓」——用土石堆起来、封住死者的地方 → 坟墓、陵墓

root: 希腊 tymbos「坟丘」（与意为「鼓起」的动词相关）→ 拉丁 tumba → 古法语 tombe → 英语 tomb。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one structure: a mound becomes a stone grave, then a royal monument, an inner chamber, a container, a recorded unit, a holy site, one room underground and finally any fatal place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座构筑展开：土丘变成石墓，再变成王陵、内部墓室、容器、记录单位、圣地、地下单室，最后变成任何致命之处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone door cut into a hillside, a name above it, darkness behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡上凿出的石墓门，门楣上有名字，门后是黑暗。

branches.en: FROM HEAP TO MONUMENT: the mound hardens into architecture and then into public statement.
branches.cn: 从土堆到纪念物：坟丘硬化成建筑，再变成公共宣示。

branches.en: ROOM AND BOX: inside the tomb is a chamber, and a small enough chamber becomes a container.
branches.cn: 房间与箱子：墓内是房间，而足够小的房间就变成容器。

branches.en: THE UNIT: excavation gives the whole structure a number and a plan.
branches.cn: 单位：发掘给整座构筑一个编号与一张平面图。

branches.en: SACRED AND UNDERGROUND: pilgrimage and catacombs multiply the forms a tomb can take.
branches.cn: 神圣与地下：朝圣与地下墓穴让墓的形式倍增。

branches.en: THE FATAL PLACE: any ending can be imagined as a tomb.
branches.cn: 致命之处：任何终结都可以被想象成一座墓。

intro.en: Tomb is a borrowed word with little internal structure in English, but its Latin and Greek ancestry connects it to a few relatives.
intro.cn: tomb 是一个借词，在英语内部结构很少，但其拉丁与希腊来历把它与少数亲属词连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Greek tymbos became Latin tumba and then English tomb; the same Latin stock gives tumulus and entomb. The Greek word is also linked to a verb for swelling.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 tymbos 变成拉丁 tumba，再进入英语 tomb；同一拉丁词干还产生 tumulus 与 entomb。这个希腊词也与一个意为「鼓起」的动词相关。

items.meaning: a mound raised over a grave
items.example: Tymbos names the heap before it names the building.
items.exampleCN: tymbos 先指土堆，后指建筑。

items.example: Latin tumba carried the word westward.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 tumba 把这个词带向西方。

items.example: Old French tombe entered English after the Conquest.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 tombe 在征服之后进入英语。

items.structure: tomb (English noun, from Old French tombe)
items.meaning: a grave or built burial structure
items.example: The tomb was cut into the rock.

items.meaning: the stone that marks a tomb
items.example: The tombstone carries a name and a date.

items.structure: en- (in) + tomb (to put in a tomb)
items.example: The body was entombed beneath the floor.

items.meaning: the act of placing in a tomb
items.example: The entombment was recorded in the parish book.
items.exampleCN: 入葬记录在教区簿册中。
这座坟丘覆盖着数座墓。

items.example: The tombal inscription is worn away.

definition_en: the planting of trees to create a forest on land that was not recently wooded
core_image: 一片裸露的坡地被成排幼树覆盖，树苗的护套排成网格
scene: 裸露的坡地上，人们按网格栽下成排树苗，护套在风里直立。 The project's afforestation covered the bare slope within five years.
sceneCN: 这里 afforestation 指「在原本无林或长期无林的土地上造林」（第 1 个义项：通过栽种树木建立新的森林覆盖）；句意为该项目的造林工程在五年内覆盖了这片裸坡。图中可辨识物件：树苗、护套、网格状栽植线、坡地。

senses.title: Planting trees to make a new forest
senses.definition: the deliberate planting of trees on bare or long-cleared land so that a forest develops
senses.definitionCN: 在裸露或长期清除过的土地上刻意栽树，使森林得以形成
senses.example: The project's afforestation covered the bare slope within five years.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目的造林工程在五年内覆盖了这片裸坡。
senses.why: ad- 'to' plus forest plus -ation: the act of turning land into forest, so the noun names the conversion.
senses.whyCN: ad-「向」加 forest 加 -ation：把土地变成森林的行为，因此名词命名的是这种转变。

senses.title: A government programme
senses.definition: a public scheme with targets, subsidies and nurseries for planting trees
senses.definitionCN: 带有目标、补贴与苗圃的公共植树计划
senses.example: The national afforestation programme hired village crews.
senses.exampleCN: 国家造林计划雇用了村庄里的作业队。
senses.why: a practice becomes a programme when a state sets a target and pays for seedlings.
senses.whyCN: 当国家设定目标并为树苗付费，一种做法就变成一项计划。

senses.title: Restoring degraded land
senses.definition: the use of tree cover to hold soil, shade crops and slow erosion on worn-out land
senses.definitionCN: 在退化土地上用树冠固土、遮荫作物并减缓侵蚀
senses.example: Afforestation stabilized the sand dunes along the road.
senses.exampleCN: 造林稳定了公路旁的沙丘。
senses.why: once land is worn out, trees are a tool for repairing its surface and water cycle.
senses.whyCN: 土地一旦退化，树木就成了修复地表与水分循环的工具。

senses.title: A carbon-removal measure
senses.definition: tree planting counted as a way to take carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把植树计为从大气中移除二氧化碳的一种方式
senses.example: The firm bought afforestation credits to offset its flights.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司购买造林信用来抵消其航班排放。
senses.why: growing trees store carbon in wood, so planting becomes a measurable climate instrument.
senses.whyCN: 生长的树把碳储存在木质中，因此植树成为可测量的气候工具。

senses.title: Urban and shelterbelt planting
senses.definition: the planting of tree belts to shade streets, block wind or hold a city's edge
senses.definitionCN: 种植树带以遮荫街道、挡风或界定城市边缘
senses.example: Afforestation along the ring road cut dust by half.
senses.exampleCN: 环城路旁的造林把扬尘减少了一半。
senses.why: the same act is used at the scale of streets and field edges, where a line of trees does the work of a forest.
senses.whyCN: 同一行为也用于街道与田边尺度，那里一排树就起到森林的作用。

senses.title: Establishing a commercial plantation
senses.definition: the planting of fast-growing trees as a crop for timber, pulp or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 把速生树当作木材、纸浆或燃料作物来种植
senses.example: Afforestation for pulp replaced part of the native scrub.
senses.exampleCN: 为纸浆而进行的造林取代了一部分原生灌丛。
senses.why: industry calls a planted crop a forest too, so the word also names plantation establishment.
senses.whyCN: 产业也把人种的作物叫作森林，因此这个词也指人工林建设。

senses.title: The technical contrast with reforestation
senses.definition: the technical label for planting on land that was not forest in the recent past, as opposed to replanting a cleared forest
senses.definitionCN: 指在近期内并非林地的土地上造林，以区别于在被砍伐的林地上重新植树
senses.example: The inventory separates afforestation from reforestation.
senses.exampleCN: 这份清单把造林与再造林分开。
senses.why: climate accounting needs a sharp line between adding new forest and replacing lost forest, and this is the line.
senses.whyCN: 气候核算需要在「新增森林」与「替代失去的森林」之间划清界线，这就是那条界线。

senses.title: Building cover where none existed
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：在原本无覆盖处建立覆盖
senses.definition: any deliberate building of a canopy-like layer over an exposed system
senses.definitionCN: 任何在裸露系统上有意建立冠层式覆盖的行为
senses.example: The team called its data afforestation a canopy over the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把自己的数据造林称作档案上的一层树冠。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the shape of planting a cover on bare ground, so it fits metadata, shade and insulation.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留「在裸地上种覆盖」的形态，因此适用于元数据、遮荫与隔热。

intro.en: Afforestation comes from Medieval Latin afforestare 'to bring land into forest', built on ad- 'to' and forestis, a Late Latin word for woodland outside a park. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: afforestation 来自中世纪拉丁 afforestare「把土地纳入森林」，由 ad-「向」与 forestis 构成；forestis 是晚期拉丁语中指公园外林地的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Foris meant 'outside, out of doors', related to fores 'door'. The image is the ground beyond the gate.
items.cn: foris 意为「外面、户外」，与 fores「门」有关。意象是门外的土地。

items.en: Forestis silva meant 'woodland outside the walls of a park', the open wooded ground reserved for hunting.
items.cn: forestis silva 意为「公园围墙之外的林地」，即留作狩猎的开阔林地。

items.en: Old French forest named a large wooded tract, often a royal hunting preserve, and passed into English as forest.
items.cn: 古法语 forest 指大片林地，常为王室猎场，后进入英语成为 forest。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus forestis produced afforestare, first a legal act: to bring land under forest law, not necessarily to plant trees.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 forestis 构成 afforestare，最初是法律行为：把土地纳入森林法，不一定栽树。

items.en: English afforest first carried the legal sense, and the modern sense of planting trees developed later.
items.cn: 英语 afforest 最初承袭法律义，现代「栽树」义较晚才发展出来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of afforestation in the planting sense is not fixed, and the legal and planting senses overlap in early records.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：afforestation 在「栽树」义上的确切首见时间没有定说，早期记录中法律义与栽植义互相交叠。

note.en: Group one holds forest words that differ by prefix and are routinely confused; group two holds related land-cover practices.
note.cn: 第一组是前缀不同、常被混淆的森林词；第二组是相关的土地覆盖做法。

entries.definition: Replanting trees on land that was forest until recently; afforestation instead starts from land that was not forest.
entries.definitionCN: 在近期仍是林地的土地上重新植树；afforestation 则从非林地开始。

entries.definition: The clearing of forest, the opposite act; the two words are often paired in climate reports.
entries.definitionCN: 清除森林，是相反的行为；两个词常在气候报告中并列出现。

entries.definition: A general word for establishing forest, covering both planting new and replanting old.
entries.definitionCN: 建立森林的统称，涵盖新造与重植两种情况。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to plant with trees or to bring under forest; the noun names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 意为栽树或使成为林地的动词；名词命名这一活动。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for putting trees in the ground, at any scale; afforestation implies a forest result.
entries.definitionCN: 指把树栽进土里的日常说法，任何规模皆可；afforestation 暗示形成森林的结果。

entries.definition: The cultivation and management of trees as a crop; it is the discipline behind afforestation.
entries.definitionCN: 把树木作为作物来培育与管理的学问；它是造林背后的学科。

entries.definition: Making damaged land usable again, by any means; tree planting is only one method.
entries.definitionCN: 用任何手段使受损土地重新可用；植树只是其中一种方法。

entries.definition: A system that absorbs more carbon than it releases; a new forest may become one.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收碳多于释放碳的系统；新森林可以成为其中之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ad- 'to' + forest + -ation: the act of turning land to forest.
normal.cn: ad-「向」+ forest + -ation：把土地变成森林的行为。

normal.en: The prefix pair tells the story: afforestation adds forest, reforestation adds it back, deforestation takes it away.
normal.cn: 前缀三兄弟讲清方向：afforestation 新增森林，reforestation 补回森林，deforestation 拿走森林。

normal.en: The family runs afforest, afforested, forest, forestry, reforestation, deforestation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 afforest、afforested、forest、forestry、reforestation、deforestation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: afforestation project, afforestation programme, afforestation rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：造林项目、造林计划、造林率。

normal.en: Forestis meant land outside the park wall, so afforestation originally meant bringing land under forest law.
normal.cn: forestis 指公园墙外的土地，因此 afforestation 最初指把土地纳入森林法。

abstract.en: Picture a green blanket sewn onto a bare hill stitch by stitch.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿毯被一针一针缝到光秃的山坡上。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of tiny umbrellas that will grow into a roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一片小伞排成网格，日后长成屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture a field learning to cast shade on itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田学会为自己投下阴影。

examples.en: Afforestation on the plateau slowed the wind erosion.
examples.cn: 高原上的造林减缓了风蚀。

examples.en: The plan promises afforestation of one million hectares.
examples.cn: 该计划承诺造林一百万公顷。

examples.en: Critics note that afforestation can lower stream flow.
examples.cn: 批评者指出，造林可能减少河流流量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「af（向）+ forest（森林）+ ation（行为）」——把土地变成森林 → 造林

root: ad-「向」+ forest + -ation；forest 经古法语来自晚期拉丁 forestis silva「公园墙外的林地」，再上溯拉丁 foris「外面」，与 fores「门」有关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: bare land is planted, seedlings close into rows, a canopy forms, and the same noun then names a state programme, a repair method, a carbon tool, an urban belt, a plantation, a technical contrast and finally any added cover.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：裸地被栽种、树苗连成行、树冠形成，随后同一名词用来命名国家计划、修复方法、碳工具、城市林带、人工林、技术区分，最后指任何新增覆盖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bare slope planted with a grid of young trees in protective sleeves.
core.cn: 核心意象：裸坡上按网格栽满带护套的幼树。

branches.en: THE BASE ACT: new forest is created, and the technical line separates it from replanting an old forest.
branches.cn: 基本行为：新森林被造出，技术界线把它与重植旧林分开。

branches.en: PROGRAMME: targets, subsidies and nurseries turn planting into public policy.
branches.cn: 计划：目标、补贴与苗圃把栽植变成公共政策。

branches.en: REPAIR AND BELT: trees hold worn soil and line streets as shelter.
branches.cn: 修复与林带：树木固住退化土壤，也沿街成带。

branches.en: CARBON AND CROP: growing wood stores carbon, and fast-growing trees become a harvest.
branches.cn: 碳与作物：生长的木质储存碳，速生树也成为收成。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any exposed system can be given a canopy of cover.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何裸露系统都可被加上一层冠盖。

intro.en: Afforestation is a Latin-derived noun with a transparent build: a prefix of direction, a forest root and a suffix of action. The family is large and mostly legal or botanical in origin.
intro.cn: afforestation 是一个拉丁来源名词，构造透明：方向前缀、森林词根与动作后缀。词族庞大，来源多为法律或植物学。

latinIntro.en: Latin foris 'outside' and forestis 'woodland outside the park' give forest; afforestare adds ad- 'to'; -atio supplies the action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 foris「外面」与 forestis「公园外林地」衍生 forest；afforestare 加 ad-「向」；-atio 提供动作名词。

火灾之后进行了再造林。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 公园外林地的；林木覆盖的

definition_zh: 财政的；政府收支与税收的；（苏格兰、西班牙等）检察官的
definition_en: relating to government money, especially taxes and public spending
core_image: 一只公家的钱箱，进账口贴着税单，出账口接向街道的公共工程
scene: 预算草案把新增收入全部投向乡镇诊所，财政官员称这是本年度最优先的支出。 The draft sent all new revenue to rural clinics, which the fiscal officers called the year's first priority.
sceneCN: 这里指「与政府收支及税收有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于国家财政收入与支出的事务）；句意为预算草案把新增收入全部投向乡镇诊所，财政官员称这是本年度最优先的支出。可辨识物件：钱箱、税单、诊所图纸、预算册。
