senses.title: Relating to government revenue and spending
senses.titleCN: 与政府收入及支出有关
senses.definition: concerning the money a government raises through taxes and spends on public needs
senses.definitionCN: 关于政府以税收取得、并用于公共需要的钱
senses.example: The fiscal cost of the programme was spread over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该计划的财政成本被分摊到十年之间。
senses.why: the word descends from the Latin word for a money basket, so whatever is fiscal belongs to the public purse rather than a private one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词上溯拉丁语中「钱筐」的说法，因此凡是财政的，都属公家钱袋而非私人钱包。

senses.title: The twelve-month accounting period
senses.titleCN: 财政年度这一十二个月的账期
senses.definition: the year a government or firm uses for budgeting and accounts, which need not begin in January
senses.definitionCN: 政府或企业用于预算与记账的年度，未必从一月开始
senses.example: The fiscal year closes at the end of March for many public bodies.
senses.exampleCN: 许多公共机构的财政年度在三月底结束。
senses.why: because accounts must be closed somewhere, the adjective attaches to the period chosen, giving a fixed label to an arbitrary calendar span.
senses.whyCN: 账目总要在某处结清，这个形容词于是附着在被选定的期间上，为一个任意的日历跨度提供固定标签。

senses.title: The balance of the public budget
senses.definition: describing whether a government is running a surplus, a balance or a deficit
senses.definitionCN: 描述政府处于盈余、平衡还是赤字状态
senses.example: The country entered the crisis with a fiscal surplus of two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 该国带着相当于经济总量百分之二的财政盈余进入危机。
senses.why: once taxes and spending are counted, the difference is a fact about the public purse, so the adjective names the state of that balance.
senses.whyCN: 税收与支出算清之后，差额成为公家钱袋的事实，这个形容词便指该差额的状态。

senses.title: Fiscal discipline and restraint
senses.definition: the practice of keeping spending and borrowing inside agreed limits
senses.definitionCN: 把支出与借款保持在约定限度内的做法
senses.example: Fiscal discipline required the ministry to refuse the extra request.
senses.exampleCN: 财政纪律要求该部拒绝这笔额外申请。
senses.why: the word can be pressed into service as a norm, not only a description, which is why it appears beside discipline and restraint.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以被当作规范使用，而不只是描述，因此常与纪律、约束一类词并置。

senses.title: Fiscal stimulus by spending or cutting tax
senses.titleCN: 以增支或减税作财政刺激
senses.definition: a deliberate expansion of the budget to raise demand during a slowdown
senses.definitionCN: 在放缓时期有意扩大预算以提高需求
senses.example: The fiscal stimulus arrived late but was large enough to shorten the recession.
senses.exampleCN: 财政刺激来得迟，但规模足以缩短衰退。
senses.why: when private demand falls, the public budget can take its place for a season, so extra spending is the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 私人需求下滑时，公共预算可以暂时替代它，额外支出于是成为工具。

senses.title: The fiscal burden on taxpayers
senses.titleCN: 纳税人承受的财政负担
senses.definition: the weight of taxes and contributions that households and firms must carry
senses.definitionCN: 家庭与企业必须承担的税收与缴费之重
senses.example: Officials argued that the fiscal burden already discouraged hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 官员认为财政负担已经在抑制招聘。
senses.why: every tax is a claim on private income, so the same budget that funds services also weighs on those who pay.
senses.whyCN: 每一项税都是对私人收入的索取，因此供给公共服务的同一预算也压在被征者身上。

senses.title: A revenue stamp or fiscal mark
senses.definition: an official stamp showing that a tax on a document has been paid
senses.definitionCN: 表明某份文书已缴税的官方印花
senses.example: The deed carried a fiscal stamp in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据的角上贴着财政印花。
senses.why: taxing papers required a visible proof of payment, so the adjective came to name the mark as well as the treasury behind it.
senses.whyCN: 对文书征税需要看得见的缴款凭证，这个形容词于是既指国库，也指那个印记。

senses.title: A public prosecutor in some legal systems
senses.definition: the official who prosecutes on behalf of the state, as in Scots and Spanish practice
senses.definitionCN: 代表国家提起公诉的官员，如苏格兰与西班牙的用法
senses.example: The fiscal presented the evidence to the court.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官向法庭提交了证据。
senses.why: the prosecutor was originally the treasury's lawyer, so the same word for the purse produced a title for the state's advocate.
senses.whyCN: 检察官最初是国库的律师，因此同一个表示钱袋的词也产出了国家公诉人的头衔。

intro.en: Fiscal comes from Latin fiscalis 'of the fiscus', the basket or chest that held public money. English borrowed it through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fiscal 来自拉丁 fiscalis「属于 fiscus 的」，fiscus 原指盛公款的篮子或钱箱。英语于 16 世纪经法语借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fiscus first meant a woven basket, then the chest in which the Roman treasury kept its money, and finally the treasury itself as an institution.
items.cn: fiscus 先指编织的篮子，后指罗马国库存放钱款的钱箱，最后指作为机构的国库本身。

items.en: The adjective fiscalis 'of the treasury' described officials, taxes and property belonging to the public chest rather than to the emperor's private purse.
items.cn: 形容词 fiscalis「国库的」描述属于公家钱箱而非皇帝私产的官员、税收与财物。

items.en: Old French fiscal carried the word into English in the sixteenth century, at first in legal writing about the royal treasury.
items.cn: 古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪把这个词带进英语，最初见于关于王室国库的法律文书。

items.en: By the eighteenth century fiscal was used broadly for taxes, debt and budgeting, and the phrase fiscal year took its modern meaning in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，fiscal 已广泛用于税收、债务与预算；「财政年度」一语在 19 世纪取得现代含义。

items.en: In legal systems where the state's advocate acted for the treasury, fiscal became a title for the public prosecutor, a sense still current in Scotland and Spain.
items.cn: 在国家公诉人代国库行事的法系中，fiscal 成为检察官的头衔，这一义在苏格兰与西班牙仍在使用。

items.en: The revenue stamp sense arose because a taxed document needed a visible mark, so the adjective named the proof of payment as well as the office behind it.
items.cn: 印花义的产生，是因为被征税的文书需要看得见的标记，形容词于是既指缴款凭证，也指其背后的机关。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from the treasury root or the same budget field; group two holds adjectives that are often used where fiscal belongs.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「国库」词根或同属预算领域的形近词；第二组是常被用在 fiscal 位置上的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The treasury or public purse itself, an archaic noun; fiscal describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指国库或公家钱袋本身，是古旧名词；fiscal 描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: In financial terms, especially of public money; it modifies an action rather than naming a field.
entries.definitionCN: 指从财政角度，尤指公款；它修饰动作，而非命名领域。

entries.definition: To take property into the public chest as a penalty; the root is the same money basket.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为处罚把财物收进公家钱箱；词根正是那只钱筐。

entries.definition: Relating to the body or to matter, from a different Greek root; it shares only a sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体的或物质的，出自另一希腊词根；仅读音相近。

entries.definition: Relating to money and finance in general, including private firms; fiscal is reserved for public money.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指金钱与金融，包含私人企业；fiscal 专指公款。

entries.definition: Relating to money supply and currency; fiscal concerns taxing and spending by the government.
entries.definitionCN: 指货币供应与通货；fiscal 关乎政府的征税与支出。

entries.definition: Relating to a budget as a plan; fiscal can describe the whole year's accounts and the treasury behind them.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为计划的预算；fiscal 可以描述整年账目及其背后的国库。

entries.definition: Relating to money as a medium, often in legal writing about loss; it lacks the public-purse sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为媒介的金钱，常用于关于损失的法律文书；不含公家钱袋义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The basket is still inside the word: a woven chest where the state keeps its money.
normal.cn: 那只篮子仍在词里：国家存钱的编织箱。

normal.en: The family runs fisc, fiscal, fiscally, confiscate, confiscation, fiscal year.
normal.cn: 同族词包括国库、财政的、在财政上、没收、充公、财政年度。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the budget: fiscal year, fiscal deficit, fiscal discipline, fiscal stimulus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出预算的各个方面：财政年度、财政赤字、财政纪律、财政刺激。

normal.en: Confiscate is the same root used as a penalty: the property goes into the public chest.
normal.cn: 没收是同一词根用作处罚：财物被收进公家钱箱。

normal.en: In Scotland a fiscal is a prosecutor because the state's lawyer once acted for the treasury.
normal.cn: 在苏格兰，检察官也被叫作这个词，因为国家律师曾代国库行事。

abstract.en: Picture one chest with a tax bill going in at the top and a road coming out at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱箱，上面进税单，下面出一条公路。

abstract.en: Picture a household calendar whose year ends in March, not December.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，年份在三月底而非十二月底结束。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp in the corner of a deed, small but able to stop a sale.
abstract.cn: 想象契据角上的一枚印花，虽小却能拦住一笔买卖。

examples.en: The fiscal cost of the war outlasted the fighting by a generation.
examples.cn: 这场战争的财政代价在战事结束后还延续了一代人。

examples.en: Fiscal rules were tightened after the deficit exceeded the legal limit.
examples.cn: 赤字超过法定上限后，财政规则被收紧。

examples.en: The fiscal year ends in June, so the accounts close before the summer recess.
examples.cn: 财政年度在六月结束，账目在夏季休会前结清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「钱筐」——公家把钱装进筐里，进的是税、出的是公共开支 → 财政的

root: 拉丁 fiscus 原指编织篮，后指罗马国库的钱箱，再指国库机构；形容词 fiscalis「国库的」经古法语 fiscal 于 16 世纪入英语。同根词有 confiscate、confiscation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chest: what goes into it, the year it is counted over, the balance left at the end, the discipline of not overdrawing it, extra spending in a slump, the weight on those who fill it, the stamp that proves a tax was paid, and the lawyer who once spoke for it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一只钱箱：装进去的东西、按什么年度结账、年终剩下的差额、不透支的纪律、衰退时的额外支出、向填箱者施加的重量、证明缴税的印花，以及曾替它说话的律师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public chest with a tax bill entering at the top and a public work leaving at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只公家钱箱，上面进税单，下面出公共工程。

branches.en: THE PURSE AND ITS WEIGHT: what belongs to the chest, and what it costs those who fill it.
branches.cn: 钱袋与重量：属于钱箱的东西，以及填箱者为此付出的代价。

branches.en: THE COUNTING PERIOD: a chosen twelve months in which income and outgo are closed off.
branches.cn: 结算期间：被选定的十二个月，在此之内结清收入与支出。

branches.en: BALANCE AND DISCIPLINE: the difference at year end, and the rule against overdrawing it.
branches.cn: 差额与纪律：年终的差额，以及不得透支的规则。

branches.en: DELIBERATE EXPANSION: in a slump the chest is opened wider on purpose.
branches.cn: 有意扩张：衰退时故意把钱箱开得更大。

branches.en: PROOF AND ADVOCATE: the stamp proves the tax was paid, and the prosecutor once spoke for the chest.
branches.cn: 凭证与代言人：印花证明税已缴，检察官曾替钱箱说话。

intro.en: Fiscal is a Latin adjective from the word for the public money chest; the root also gives the verb for taking property into that chest.
intro.cn: fiscal 是由「公家钱箱」一词派生的拉丁形容词；同一词根还给出「把财物收进钱箱」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fiscus and fiscalis stand behind fiscal, fisc and confiscate; the basket is the common image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fiscus 与 fiscalis 支撑 fiscal、fisc 与 confiscate；那只篮子是他们共同的意象。

items.example: The chest held the province's revenue.
items.exampleCN: 这只钱箱装着该省的税收。
该计划在财政上是中性的。

items.meaning: to take into the public chest
the act of taking into the chest

items.example: The fiscal year ends in March.

items.exampleCN: 改革后财政状况有所改善。
财政学者争论这条规则。

latinEntries.meaning: to lay up in the chest, confiscate

definition_zh: 伪装的；保护色的；隐蔽的
definition_en: made to blend into the surroundings so that it is hard to see or recognise
core_image: 一只停在树皮上的蛾，翅上的斑纹与树皮纹理严丝合缝
scene: 雨后的林地，一只蛾停在长满苔藓的树干上，翅上的纹路与树皮几乎一致。 The moth is camouflaged against the mossy bark.
sceneCN: 这里 camouflaged 指「颜色或斑纹与背景一致，使物体难以被发现」（第 1 个义项：外观与周围环境相合而隐藏起来）；句意为这只蛾贴在长满苔藓的树皮上，因与背景同色而不易被看见。图中可辨识物件：蛾、苔藓树皮、翅面斑纹。

pos.zh: 伪装的；保护色的；隐蔽的（常作表语或前置定语）
camouflage 的过去式与过去分词：把……伪装起来

senses.title: Blend into natural surroundings
senses.definition: having colours or patterns that match the background so that an animal is hard to detect
senses.definitionCN: 颜色或斑纹与背景一致，使动物难以被发现
senses.example: The moth is camouflaged against the mossy bark.
senses.exampleCN: 这只蛾贴在长满苔藓的树皮上，与背景融为一体。
senses.why: The ending -ed states the result of camouflage: the surface has been made to copy what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ed 表示伪装的结果：表面已经被做成与背后的东西相似。

senses.title: Conceal military equipment
senses.definition: covered or painted so that troops, vehicles or positions cannot be seen from a distance or from the air
senses.definitionCN: 用网、树枝或涂料遮盖，使部队、车辆或阵地无法从远处或空中被看见
senses.example: The artillery battery was camouflaged with netting and cut branches.
senses.exampleCN: 炮兵阵地用伪装网和砍下的树枝掩蔽起来。
senses.why: Modern camouflage began as a military problem: artillery and aircraft made any visible target fatal, so hiding shape and colour became a tactic.
senses.whyCN: 现代伪装最初是军事问题：火炮与飞机让任何暴露的目标都变得致命，于是隐藏形状与颜色成了一种战术。

senses.title: Disguise an object as another kind
senses.titleCN: 把物件伪装成别的东西
senses.definition: made to look like something ordinary so that observers do not recognise it for what it is
senses.definitionCN: 把物件做成普通事物的样子，使观察者认不出它的本来面目
senses.example: The truck was camouflaged to look like a delivery van.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆卡车被伪装成一辆送货车。
senses.why: Once hiding by appearance was established, disguising a whole object as a different object was a short practical step.
senses.whyCN: 一旦按外观隐藏的思路确立，把整个物件伪装成另一种物件只是顺理成章的实用一步。

senses.title: Mask an intention or feeling
senses.definition: used of words, behaviour or expressions that hide what someone really means or feels
senses.definitionCN: 形容言辞、行为或表情掩盖真实意思或感受
senses.example: His polite phrasing camouflaged a blunt refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 他客气的措辞掩饰了一个生硬的拒绝。
senses.why: What works for surfaces in war also works for speech: a friendly outer layer can cover a hostile content.
senses.whyCN: 战时的表面伪装同样适用于言语：友善的外层可以遮住敌对的内容。

senses.title: Wearing camouflage-patterned gear
senses.titleCN: 穿着迷彩图案的衣物或装备
senses.definition: made of fabric or material printed with a camouflage pattern
senses.definitionCN: 由印有迷彩图案的布料或材料制成
senses.example: Soldiers in camouflaged jackets moved along the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 身穿迷彩夹克的士兵沿着山脊移动。
senses.why: The pattern took its name from the noun, so anything printed with it is described by the same participle.
senses.whyCN: 这种图案沿用了名词 camouflage 的名称，因此印有该图案的物品也用同一个分词来形容。

senses.title: Shield eggs or young by matching the nest
senses.titleCN: 以巢穴配色护住卵或幼体
senses.definition: used of eggs, nests or young whose appearance matches the ground so that predators overlook them
senses.definitionCN: 形容卵、巢或幼体外观与地面一致，使捕食者忽略它们
senses.example: The camouflaged eggs survive better on speckled gravel than on plain sand.
senses.exampleCN: 这些伪装色的卵在斑驳的砾石上比在纯色沙地上存活得更好。
senses.why: Protective resemblance extends from the parent's body to the clutch, so the same adjective covers eggs and nests.
senses.whyCN: 保护性相似从亲本体表延伸到整窝卵，因此同一个形容词也用于卵与巢。

senses.title: Hide an installation in plain sight
senses.titleCN: 让设施隐身于寻常景观
senses.definition: used of buildings or sites designed to look ordinary so that they escape notice
senses.definitionCN: 形容建筑或场地被设计成寻常样子，从而不引起注意
senses.example: The office block was camouflaged as a warehouse to hide the laboratory inside.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋办公楼被伪装成仓库，以遮住里面的实验室。
senses.why: Military concealment scaled up to whole sites: a building can wear an ordinary face.
senses.whyCN: 军事隐蔽放大到整个场地：一栋建筑可以戴上一张寻常的脸。

senses.title: Disguise network traffic or signals
senses.definition: used of data or signals altered to look like ordinary traffic so that monitoring does not flag them
senses.definitionCN: 形容数据或信号被改造成普通流量的样子，使监测不予标记
senses.example: The messages were camouflaged as routine software updates.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信息被伪装成常规的软件更新。
senses.why: The newest extension keeps the same logic: hide the real content inside an expected pattern.
senses.whyCN: 最新的引申保持同一逻辑：把真实内容藏进一个可预期的模式里。

intro.en: Camouflaged is the past participle of camouflage, a word English borrowed from French military slang during the First World War; French took it from Italian. No Latin etymon can be recovered, so the Latin list is empty.
intro.cn: camouflaged 是 camouflage 的过去分词；camouflage 是第一次世界大战期间英语从法语军事俚语借入的词，法语又取自意大利语。无法追溯到可靠的拉丁词源，故拉丁条目留空。

items.en: Italian camuffare 'to disguise, to trick' is the earliest traceable form, recorded in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 意大利语 camuffare「伪装、欺骗」是最早可追溯的形式，见于 19 世纪。

items.en: French slang camoufler 'to disguise' entered military speech around 1915, apparently from the Italian verb.
items.cn: 法语俚语 camoufler「伪装」约在 1915 年进入军人用语，一般认为来自上述意大利语动词。

items.en: English adopted camouflage in 1917, when the concealment of guns and aircraft became an official concern; the participle camouflaged appeared at the same time.
items.cn: 英语在 1917 年借入 camouflage，当时火炮与飞机的隐蔽成为官方要务；分词 camouflaged 同时出现。

items.en: The French noun camouflage used -age, a suffix of action or result, and English kept the noun unchanged.
items.cn: 法语名词 camouflage 使用表示行为或结果的后缀 -age，英语把这个名词原样保留。

items.en: By the mid twentieth century camouflaged extended from bodies and vehicles to intentions, institutions and transmitted signals.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪中叶，camouflaged 已从身体与车辆扩展到意图、机构与传输信号。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the deeper origin of Italian camuffare is disputed; one hypothesis links it to muffare 'to muffle', another to a dialect word for a mask, and no Latin etymon can be established. Only the first printed dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：意大利语 camuffare 的更深来源有争议，一说与 muffare「捂住」有关，一说与某种方言中表示面具的词有关，无法确立拉丁词源；仅首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the base form and its immediate derivatives, which are easy to confuse with the participle; group two holds near synonyms that differ in how openly or how completely the hiding is done.
note.cn: 第一组是本词原形及其直接派生形式，容易与这个分词混用；第二组是近义词，区别在于隐藏的公开程度与彻底程度。

entries.definition: The verb or the thing itself, not the resulting state; camouflaged describes something after the act has been done.
entries.definitionCN: 指动词或伪装这一事物本身，而非结果状态；camouflaged 描述行为完成后的样子。

entries.definition: The present participle, naming the act while it happens; camouflaged names the finished condition.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，指正在进行的动作；camouflaged 指完成后的状态。

entries.definition: A person who designs camouflage; it is an agent noun and never describes the hidden object.
entries.definitionCN: 指设计伪装的人；是施动名词，从不形容被隐藏的物件。

entries.definition: The printed design itself; a camouflaged jacket is a jacket made with that design.
entries.definitionCN: 指图案本身；camouflaged jacket 指用该图案制成的夹克。

entries.definition: Made to look like another person or thing; it stresses a false identity more than a merge with the background.
entries.definitionCN: 指被改扮成另一个人或物；更强调假身份，而非与背景融合。

entries.definition: Deliberately kept out of sight; it says nothing about matching colours or patterns.
entries.definitionCN: 指被有意藏起来看不见；不涉及颜色或斑纹是否相合。

entries.definition: Covered by something that hides the surface; the emphasis falls on a covering layer rather than on resemblance.
entries.definitionCN: 指被某物覆盖而遮住表面；重点在覆盖层，而不在相似。

entries.definition: Merged into the surroundings without sharp edges; it describes visual mixing, not a deliberate military act.
entries.definitionCN: 指与周围柔和地融在一起、没有明显边界；描述视觉混合，不含刻意的军事行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real French and Italian lineage, the real derivatives, and the fixed phrases that military writers actually use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的法语与意大利语来源、真实的派生词，以及军事写作中实际使用的固定搭配。

normal.en: camouflage plus -ed: the state of having been disguised.
normal.cn: camouflage 加 -ed：已经伪装好的状态。

normal.en: The family runs camouflage, camouflaged, camouflaging, camoufleur.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 camouflage、camouflaged、camouflaging、camoufleur。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: heavily camouflaged, camouflaged vehicle, camouflaged position.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 heavily camouflaged、camouflaged vehicle、camouflaged position。

normal.en: The word entered English in 1917, from French military slang.
normal.cn: 这个词 1917 年从法语军事俚语进入英语。

normal.en: Three scales to remember: an animal's skin, a vehicle's paint, a building's facade.
normal.cn: 可按三个尺度记忆：动物的皮肤、车辆的漆面、建筑的外立面。

abstract.en: Picture a moth whose wings repeat the bark grain so exactly that the eye slides off it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蛾，翅膀把树皮纹理重复得如此精确，目光会从它身上滑过去。

abstract.en: Picture a tank wearing a coat of branches and reading as a hedge.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆坦克披着树枝，看上去像一道树篱。

abstract.en: Picture a polite sentence standing as a painted screen in front of a refusal.
abstract.cn: 想象一句客气话像一块彩绘屏风立在拒绝之前。

examples.en: The nestlings are camouflaged by their down, which matches the lichen.
examples.cn: 雏鸟的绒羽与地衣同色，因此被伪装起来。

examples.en: Every vehicle in the convoy was camouflaged before dawn.
examples.cn: 车队里的每辆车都在天亮前完成了伪装。

examples.en: The report's calm tone camouflaged a serious warning.
examples.cn: 报告平静的语调掩盖了一个严重警告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「camouflage（伪装）+ -ed」——被伪装起来的 → 伪装色的；隐蔽的

root: 意大利语 camuffare「伪装、欺骗」（19 世纪）→ 法语俚语 camoufler → 英语 camouflage；词根来源不确定，无可考的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of hiding: an animal's surface copies its background, then vehicles, objects, speech, clothing, nests, buildings and finally data wear the same disguise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种隐藏行为展开：动物体表复制背景，随后车辆、物件、言语、衣物、巢、建筑，直到数据，都披上同一层伪装。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a moth whose wing pattern repeats the bark so closely that the eye cannot separate them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蛾的翅纹把树皮重复得如此紧密，眼睛无法把它们分开。

branches.en: NATURAL RESEMBLANCE: bodies and clutches copy the ground for survival.
branches.cn: 自然相似：身体与整窝卵复制地面以求生存。

branches.en: MILITARY DRESS: equipment and uniforms take the pattern as a tactic.
branches.cn: 军事装束：装备与制服把该图案当作战术。

branches.en: OBJECT DISGUISE: a whole thing is remade as another kind of thing.
branches.cn: 物件伪装：整个物体被改造成另一类物体。

branches.en: VERBAL MASK: polite wording covers a blunt content.
branches.cn: 言语掩饰：客气的措辞盖住生硬的内容。

branches.en: SYSTEMIC COVER: sites and data traffic are hidden inside ordinary appearances.
branches.cn: 系统性掩护：场地与数据流量被藏进寻常外观之中。

intro.en: The word is a French-derived base with an English participial ending; its parts are a verb stem plus -age and -ed, not a Latin root plus prefix.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语来源的词干加英语分词词尾；其构成为动词词干加 -age 与 -ed，而非拉丁词根加前缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin etymon is recoverable. The line runs from Italian camuffare through French camoufler to English, so the Latin entry list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: 无法追溯到拉丁词源。线索从意大利语 camuffare 经法语 camoufler 到英语，因此拉丁条目按规则留空。

items.example: Camouflage buys a unit time to move.
items.exampleCN: 伪装为一个单位争取移动的时间。

items.meaningCN: 被伪装得与背景相合的
items.example: The moth is camouflaged against the bark.
items.exampleCN: 这只蛾贴在树皮上，与背景相合。

items.example: They spent the night camouflaging the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 他们花了一夜时间伪装那座桥。

items.example: A camoufleur painted the hangar to match the hillside.
items.exampleCN: 一位伪装技师把机库漆成与山坡相合的颜色。

items.meaningCN: 用于遮蔽装备的伪装网
items.example: The crew draped a camouflage net over the gun.
items.exampleCN: 炮组把一张伪装网盖在火炮上。

items.meaning: a printed design that imitates terrain
items.example: The new camouflage pattern mixes four earth tones.
items.exampleCN: 新的迷彩图案混合了四种土色。

items.meaningCN: 降低可见度的伪装涂料
items.example: Camouflage paint dulls the shine of metal.
items.exampleCN: 伪装涂料使金属不再反光。

items.meaning: jacket printed with a camouflage design
items.example: He wore a camouflage jacket in the field.
items.exampleCN: 他在野外穿了一件迷彩夹克。

items.example: Camouflage training includes shadow and texture.
items.exampleCN: 伪装训练包括阴影与纹理的利用。

definition_zh: 染色体定位；确定基因在染色体上的位置
definition_en: the process of determining the positions of genes or markers along a chromosome
core_image: 一条长尺上标出一个个基因的刻度位置
scene: 这里指「染色体定位」。 Chromosome mapping placed the resistance gene near the end of the long arm.
sceneCN: 这里 chromosome mapping 指「染色体定位」（第 1 个义项：确定基因在染色体上的位置）；句意：染色体定位把这个抗性基因放在长臂末端附近。

pos.zh: 染色体定位；基因定位（不可数，指方法或过程；作可数时可指一次定位工作）

senses.title: Locating genes
senses.definition: the determination of where genes or DNA markers lie on a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 确定基因或 DNA 标记在染色体上的位置
senses.example: Chromosome mapping located the gene between two known markers.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体定位把这个基因落在两个已知标记之间。
senses.why: A map turns unknown territory into named positions, and here the territory is the length of a chromosome.
senses.whyCN: 地图把未知地域变成有名字的位置，而这里的地域就是一条染色体的长度。

senses.title: Linkage mapping
senses.definition: mapping by measuring how often traits are inherited together
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量性状共同遗传的频率来定位
senses.example: Linkage mapping gave a rough position before sequencing was cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 在测序还昂贵的时候，连锁定位给出了粗略的位置。
senses.why: Genes near each other tend to travel together, so co-inheritance frequencies become a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 相邻的基因倾向于一起传递，因此共同遗传的频率就成了一把尺。

senses.title: Physical mapping
senses.definition: mapping by measuring actual distances in DNA base pairs
senses.definitionCN: 以 DNA 碱基对的实际距离来定位
senses.example: Physical mapping reports distances in millions of base pairs.
senses.exampleCN: 物理定位以百万碱基对为单位报告距离。
senses.why: When the molecule itself can be measured, the ruler stops being statistical and becomes literal.
senses.whyCN: 当分子本身可以被测量时，这把尺就从统计性的变成字面意义上的。

senses.title: Ordering markers
senses.definition: the ordering of known DNA sequences along a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 把已知 DNA 序列按其在染色体上的顺序排列
senses.example: Chromosome mapping ordered the clones into a single contig.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体定位把这些克隆排成一个连续片段。
senses.why: A map is also a list in order, so mapping can mean putting fragments into their true sequence.
senses.whyCN: 地图也是一份有顺序的清单，因此定位也可以指把片段放回真实次序。

senses.title: A whole-genome project
senses.definition: a large organised effort to map all chromosomes of a species
senses.definitionCN: 为定位一个物种全部染色体而组织的大型计划
senses.example: The chromosome mapping project published its first draft in the 1990s.
senses.exampleCN: 这项染色体定位计划在 1990 年代公布了初稿。
senses.why: Science turns a method into an institution when it organises a project around it, and the phrase then names the effort.
senses.whyCN: 当科学围绕一种方法组织起计划时，方法就变成了建制，这个短语于是指那项工作本身。

senses.title: Comparing species
senses.definition: mapping used to compare chromosome arrangement across species
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较不同物种染色体排列的定位
senses.example: Chromosome mapping showed that whole blocks had been rearranged.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体定位显示整块片段发生了重排。
senses.why: If maps of two species can be laid side by side, mapping becomes a tool of evolutionary comparison.
senses.whyCN: 如果两个物种的图谱可以并排放置，定位就成了演化比较的工具。

senses.title: Clinical use
senses.definition: mapping to find the position of a disease gene for diagnosis
senses.definitionCN: 为诊断而定位疾病基因的位置
senses.example: Chromosome mapping narrowed the disease gene to a small interval.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体定位把疾病基因缩小到一个很小的区间。
senses.why: Once a disease gene has an address, a test can be designed for it, so mapping serves diagnosis.
senses.whyCN: 一旦疾病基因有了地址，就能为它设计检测，因此定位服务于诊断。

senses.title: The resulting map
senses.definition: the map produced by such work, showing positions and distances
senses.definitionCN: 由此得到的图谱，标出位置与距离
senses.example: The chromosome mapping is now available as a public database.
senses.exampleCN: 这份染色体图谱现在作为公共数据库开放。
senses.why: The activity and its product share one name, a common pattern for work that leaves a document behind.
senses.whyCN: 活动与其产物共用一个名字，这是「留下文件的工作」常见的命名方式。

intro.en: Chromosome mapping joins a Greek compound for the gene carrier to an English word for a drawn plan of the land.
intro.cn: chromosome mapping 把表示基因载体的希腊语复合词，接到一个表示绘制地形的英语词上。

items.en: Chromosome is chroma, 'colour', plus sōma, 'body', coined in German in 1888 for the dye-taking bodies seen during division.
items.cn: chromosome 是 chroma「颜色」加 sōma「身体」，1888 年在德语中造出，指分裂时吸收染料的那些小体。

items.en: Map comes from Latin mappa, 'cloth, napkin'. A mappa mundi was a cloth on which the world was drawn, and English map shortened that phrase.
items.cn: map 出自拉丁语 mappa「布、餐巾」。mappa mundi 指画着世界的那块布，英语 map 就是这一短语的缩略。

items.en: The idea of arranging genes in a linear order on chromosomes took shape in the work of Morgan's school around 1913, where linkage maps were drawn. The phrase chromosome mapping itself is later.
items.cn: 把基因按线性顺序排在染色体上的想法，在 1913 年前后 Morgan 学派的工作中成形，当时绘制了连锁图。chromosome mapping 这一短语本身出现得更晚。

items.en: In the 1980s and 1990s chromosome mapping became an organised project with physical maps measured in base pairs.
items.cn: 1980 至 1990 年代，染色体定位成为有组织的计划，物理图谱以碱基对为单位测量。

items.en: After whole-genome sequencing, mapping became largely computational, though the phrase remains standard for assigning positions.
items.cn: 全基因组测序之后，定位主要变成计算工作，但这个短语仍是「指定位置」的标准说法。

note.en: The first group separates mapping from the maps it produces and from other chromosome techniques; the second separates it from sequencing and from broader genome work.
note.cn: 第一组把定位与它产出的图谱以及其它染色体技术分开；第二组把它与测序以及更广的基因组工作分开。

entries.definition: The chart of gene positions produced by mapping; mapping is the activity, the map is the document.
entries.definitionCN: 指定位工作产出的基因位置图；mapping 是活动，map 是文件。

entries.definition: Often used interchangeably, though it stresses genes rather than the chromosome as the object being placed.
entries.definitionCN: 常可互换使用，但它强调的是基因本身，而不是承载它们的染色体。

entries.definition: Photographing and sorting a cell's full chromosome set; it shows number and shape, not the position of individual genes.
entries.definitionCN: 指拍摄并排列一个细胞的全套染色体，显示数目与形态，而不是单个基因的位置。

entries.definition: Determining the exact order of bases in DNA; it produces the letters that mapping then places on a chromosome.
entries.definitionCN: 指测定 DNA 碱基的确切顺序，产出字母序列，再由定位放回染色体。

entries.definition: The same work extended to every chromosome of an organism at once.
entries.definitionCN: 把同样的工作一次性扩展到该生物的全部染色体。

entries.definition: Using a mapped position to isolate the actual gene; mapping finds the address, cloning retrieves the text.
entries.definitionCN: 利用已定位的位置把真正的基因分离出来；定位找地址，克隆取正文。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: chromosome + mapping: drawing a map along a chromosome.
normal.cn: chromosome + mapping：沿一条染色体画地图。

normal.en: The family runs map, mapping, genetic map, physical map and linkage map.
normal.cn: 同族词有 map、mapping、genetic map、physical map、linkage map。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: linkage mapping, physical mapping, chromosome mapping project.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：连锁定位、物理定位、染色体定位计划。

normal.en: Linkage mapping measures co-inheritance; physical mapping measures base pairs.
normal.cn: 连锁定位测量共同遗传，物理定位测量碱基对。

normal.en: Mapping finds the address; sequencing reads the text.
normal.cn: 定位找地址，测序读正文。

abstract.en: Think of an old cloth map: the chromosome is the coastline, and each gene is a marked harbour.
abstract.cn: 想象一块旧布地图：染色体是海岸线，每个基因是一个标出的港口。

abstract.en: Linkage mapping is guessing distances from which travellers arrive together.
abstract.cn: 连锁定位就像靠「哪些旅人总是一起到」来推测距离。

abstract.en: A mapping project is a survey crew walking the whole length of a country.
abstract.cn: 定位计划就像一支测量队走遍一个国家的全长。

examples.en: Chromosome mapping placed the mutation within a region of two million base pairs.
examples.cn: 染色体定位把该突变落在两百万碱基对的一个区域内。

examples.en: Linkage mapping was the main tool before sequencing became affordable.
examples.cn: 在测序变得廉价之前，连锁定位是主要工具。

examples.en: The chromosome mapping data are shared through a public database.
examples.cn: 染色体定位数据通过公共数据库共享。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「chromosome（染色体）+ mapping（画地图）」→ 给染色体画地图 → 染色体定位

root: 希腊语 chroma「颜色」+ sōma「身体」→ chromosome；拉丁语 mappa「布」→ map + -ing → mapping。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the act of locating a gene, through the linkage and physical methods, the ordering of markers, the organised project, species comparison, clinical use, and finally the map itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「给基因定位」这个动作出发，经过连锁法与物理法、标记排序、有组织的计划、物种比较、临床用途，最后落到图谱本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long ruler with a gene marked at each graduation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把长尺，每个刻度上都标着一个基因。

branches.en: ACT AND PRODUCT: locating genes, and the map that results.
branches.cn: 活动与产物：给基因定位，以及由此得到的图谱。

branches.en: TWO RULERS: inheritance frequencies and literal base-pair distances.
branches.cn: 两把尺：遗传频率与字面上的碱基对距离。

branches.en: ORDER: putting known fragments into their true sequence.
branches.cn: 顺序：把已知片段放回真实次序。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND CLINIC: the organised project, and the diagnostic use of a found address.
branches.cn: 建制与临床：有组织的计划，以及用找到的地址做诊断。

branches.en: COMPARISON: laying two species' maps side by side.
branches.cn: 比较：把两个物种的图谱并排放置。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek compound noun to an English gerund; mapping carries the agent suffix -ing on a Latin borrowing.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊语复合名词接到一个英语动名词上；mapping 在拉丁语借词后带 -ing。

latinIntro.en: Greek chroma and sōma build chromosome; Latin mappa, 'cloth', gives map, and English -ing makes the activity noun.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 chroma 与 sōma 构成 chromosome；拉丁语 mappa「布」给出 map，英语 -ing 构成表示活动的名词。

items.example: Chromosome mapping took years of collaborative work.
items.exampleCN: 染色体定位耗费了多年的协作。

items.meaning: a drawing of positions; to locate
items.example: They mapped the gene to the short arm.
items.exampleCN: 他们把这个基因定位到短臂上。

items.meaning: the activity of making a map
items.example: Mapping continued after the first draft.
items.exampleCN: 初稿完成后定位工作仍在继续。

items.meaning: the tendency of genes to be inherited together
items.example: Linkage analysis placed the gene near the centromere.
items.exampleCN: 连锁分析把该基因定位在着丝粒附近。

items.meaning: a known DNA site used as a reference point
items.meaningCN: 用作参照点的已知 DNA 位点
items.exampleCN: 两个标记夹住了这个区域。

items.meaning: an unbroken stretch of assembled DNA
items.meaningCN: 拼接成连续不断的一段 DNA
items.example: The contig spans the whole arm.
items.exampleCN: 这个连续片段覆盖整条臂。

items.meaning: the chromosome set of a cell
items.meaningCN: 一个细胞的染色体组成

items.exampleCN: 测序确认了定位的位置。

items.meaningCN: 与已定位的位置有关的
items.example: Positional cloning began from the mapped interval.
items.exampleCN: 定位克隆从已定位的区间开始。

latinEntries.meaning: a cloth; the cloth on which a map was drawn

definition_zh: 海洋沉积物；海相沉积（堆积在海底的泥沙、生物残骸与化学沉淀）
definition_en: material deposited on the seafloor, including eroded rock debris, remains of organisms and chemical precipitates
core_image: 海底一层层细泥与贝壳碎片缓慢落下，越往下越压得紧实，像一本合上的厚书
scene: 钻探船把长管插进海底，提起一段层理分明的泥柱。 Layers of marine sediment record millions of years of ocean history.
sceneCN: 这里 marine sediment 指「堆积在海底的沉积物」（第 1 个义项：覆盖海底的整体沉积物）；句意为层层海洋沉积物记录了数百万年的海洋历史。

pos.zh: 海洋沉积物；海相沉积（不可数，指不同来源时可用复数 marine sediments）

derivatives.zh: marinus（拉丁「海的」）→ 海的、海生的、海洋的
sedimentum（拉丁「沉淀物」，源自 sedere「坐下」）→ 沉积物；使沉淀
sediment + -ary（形容词后缀）→ 沉积形成的：沉积岩的
sediment + -ation（动作或结果）→ 沉积作用：颗粒沉降堆积的过程
sediment + -o- + -logy（学科后缀）→ 沉积学：研究沉积物与沉积岩的学科

senses.title: The seafloor deposit as a whole
senses.definition: the aggregate of loose material covering the seafloor
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖海底的松散物质总体
senses.example: Layers of marine sediment record millions of years of ocean history.
senses.exampleCN: 层层海洋沉积物记录了数百万年的海洋历史。
senses.why: marine fixes the setting and sediment fixes the material, so the phrase names whatever has settled on the seafloor.
senses.whyCN: marine 限定环境，sediment 限定材料，短语因此命名一切沉降到海底的东西。

senses.title: Land-derived debris
senses.definition: sand, silt and clay eroded from land and carried into the sea
senses.definitionCN: 从陆地侵蚀而来、被带入海洋的砂、粉砂与黏土
senses.example: River floods deliver coarse marine sediment to the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 河流洪水把粗粒海洋沉积物送到大陆架。
senses.why: most seafloor material starts as rock on land, so the phrase often refers specifically to that eroded fraction.
senses.whyCN: 海底物质大多起于陆上岩石，因此这个短语常特指那部分被侵蚀的碎屑。

senses.title: Remains of marine organisms
senses.definition: shells, tests and soft parts of organisms that accumulate as ooze
senses.definitionCN: 以软泥形式堆积的生物贝壳、壳体与软组织
senses.example: Calcareous marine sediment is made of tiny shell debris.
senses.exampleCN: 钙质海洋沉积物由微小贝壳碎屑构成。
senses.why: in the open ocean, the dominant supply is not land but the shells of plankton falling from above.
senses.whyCN: 在开阔海洋，主要供给不是陆地，而是自上落下的浮游生物壳。

senses.title: Chemical precipitates
senses.definition: minerals formed by chemical reaction or precipitation in seawater
senses.definitionCN: 在海水中经化学反应或沉淀形成的矿物
senses.example: Manganese nodules grow within marine sediment.
senses.exampleCN: 锰结核在海洋沉积物中生长。
senses.why: seawater itself can deposit solids, so the phrase also covers material that was never a particle of rock or shell.
senses.whyCN: 海水本身也能沉淀固体，因此这个短语也涵盖从未是岩石或贝壳颗粒的物质。

senses.title: A layered archive
senses.definition: the stratified sequence read as a record of past conditions
senses.definitionCN: 作为过去环境记录来解读的层状序列
senses.example: The marine sediment sequence spans the last ice age.
senses.exampleCN: 这段海洋沉积层序跨越上一个冰期。
senses.why: deposition is ordered in time, so the pile becomes readable from bottom to top.
senses.whyCN: 沉积按时间排序，因此这堆物质可以从下往上阅读。

senses.title: A size and rate signal
senses.definition: the grain size and accumulation rate used to infer current strength and supply
senses.definitionCN: 用来推断水流强度与供给量的粒径与堆积速率
senses.example: Coarse marine sediment points to a strong bottom current.
senses.exampleCN: 粗粒海洋沉积物指向强劲的底层流。
senses.why: fast water carries coarse grains and slow water drops fine ones, so texture records the flow.
senses.whyCN: 快水搬运粗颗粒，慢水只落细颗粒，因此质地记录了流动。

senses.title: A sampling target
senses.definition: the material recovered in cores and grabs for study
senses.definitionCN: 用岩芯管与抓斗取出供研究的材料
senses.example: The core brought up two metres of marine sediment.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯管取上两米海洋沉积物。
senses.why: the phrase names both the deposit and the object a ship actually recovers, which is how field scientists use it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既命名沉积层，也命名船上实际取回的物件，野外科学家正是这样使用。

senses.title: A foundation material
senses.definition: the deposit considered for its strength and stability under structures
senses.definitionCN: 从结构与稳定性角度考虑的沉积层
senses.example: Engineers tested the marine sediment before building the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在建造平台前测试了这片海洋沉积物。
senses.why: loose seafloor material bears loads and can liquefy, so engineering treats it as a material with properties.
senses.whyCN: 松散海底物质要承受荷载也可能液化，因此工程学把它当作有性质的材料。

intro.en: Marine sediment joins a Latin adjective to a Latin noun. Marine derives from mare 'sea' through marinus; sediment derives from sedimentum 'a settling', from sedere 'to sit'. The phrase is English, but every element is Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marine sediment 把拉丁形容词接在拉丁名词上。marine 经 marinus 来自 mare「海」；sediment 来自 sedimentum「沉降物」，再上溯 sedere「坐下」。短语是英语，但每个成分都是拉丁语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mare 'sea' produced marinus 'of the sea', which French and English shortened into the adjective marine.
items.cn: mare「海」产生 marinus「海的」，法语与英语再把它简化为形容词 marine。

items.en: Sedere meant 'to sit, to settle'; its participle formed sedimentum, literally 'that which has settled'.
items.cn: sedere 意为「坐、沉降」；其分词构成 sedimentum，字面就是「已经沉下来的东西」。

items.en: Sediment entered English in the seventeenth century as a general word for matter that settles in liquid.
items.cn: sediment 于十七世纪进入英语，泛指在液体中沉降的物质。

items.en: As geology developed, sediment was extended from laboratory settling to rock debris laid down by water, wind and ice.
items.cn: 随着地质学发展，sediment 从实验室沉淀扩展到水、风与冰堆积的岩石碎屑。

items.en: Deep-sea coring in the twentieth century made marine sediment a standard term for the seafloor's layered cover.
items.cn: 二十世纪的深海取芯使 marine sediment 成为海底层状覆盖物的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the phrase's earliest technical citation is not consistently dated, though both words are securely documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：这个短语最早的技术书证各家年代不一，尽管两个词本身记载可靠。

note.en: Group one holds the sediment terms most often mixed up with marine sediment; group two holds the general words for material that settles.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 marine sediment 混淆的沉积术语；第二组是泛指沉降物质的词。

entries.definition: Rock formed from compacted sediment; marine sediment is the loose material before that hardening.
entries.definitionCN: 由沉积物压实形成的岩石；marine sediment 是压实之前的松散材料。

entries.definition: Any material laid down in the sea, including chemical and volcanic kinds; it is broader than the usual sandy meaning of sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 在海洋中堆积的任何物质，包括化学与火山来源；比通常偏砂泥含义的 sediment 更宽。

entries.definition: A deep-sea deposit made mainly of plankton remains; it is one type of marine sediment, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 主要由浮游生物遗骸构成的深海沉积；它是海洋沉积物的一种，不是整个类别。

entries.definition: Soft wet earth or clay; it can be on land, and it lacks the marine setting and the geological scope.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软潮湿的土或黏土；可以在陆上，缺少海洋环境与地质范围。

entries.definition: Material that settles in water or wind; it needs no marine qualifier and may be found in rivers or lakes.
entries.definitionCN: 在水或风中沉降的物质；无需海洋限定，也可出现在河流或湖泊中。

entries.definition: A mass of material that has accumulated, including ore and volcanic layers; it is broader and less textural than sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 已经堆积的一团物质，包括矿体与火山层；比 sediment 更宽，也更不强调质地。

entries.definition: Fine particles between sand and clay; it is a size class within sediment, not a setting.
entries.definitionCN: 介于砂与黏土之间的细颗粒；它是沉积物中的粒径等级，不是环境。

entries.definition: Scattered fragments of rock or other material; it stresses breakage rather than settling.
entries.definitionCN: 散落的岩石或其他材料碎块；强调破碎，而非沉降。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin roots, real grain sizes and real deep-sea terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的粒径与真实的深海术语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sedere means sit: sediment is what has sat down out of the water.
normal.cn: sedere 意为坐：sediment 就是从水里坐下来的东西。

normal.en: marinus means of the sea: marine marks the setting, sediment marks the material.
normal.cn: marinus 意为海的：marine 标环境，sediment 标材料。

normal.en: Three sources: land debris, plankton shells, chemical precipitate.
normal.cn: 三种来源：陆地碎屑、浮游生物壳、化学沉淀。

normal.en: Grain size order runs clay, silt, sand, gravel, and the size tells the current.
normal.cn: 粒径次序是黏土、粉砂、砂、砾，粒径告诉水流强弱。

normal.en: A core is a library: each centimetre is a page of ocean history.
normal.cn: 岩芯是一座图书馆：每一厘米都是海洋历史的一页。

abstract.en: Marine sediment is the ocean writing its diary in falling dust.
abstract.cn: 海洋沉积物是海洋用落下的尘写下日记。

abstract.en: The seafloor is a slow budget: what land loses, the deep receives.
abstract.cn: 海底是一本缓慢的账：陆地失去的，深海收下。

abstract.en: Every shell that sinks is a letter posted from the sunlit layer to the dark.
abstract.cn: 每一枚下沉的贝壳，都是从阳光层寄往黑暗层的一封信。

examples.en: The core sample contained marine sediment from the last glacial period.
examples.cn: 岩芯样品中含有上个冰期的海洋沉积物。

examples.en: Marine sediment on the slope is unstable after heavy storms.
examples.cn: 大风暴之后，斜坡上的海洋沉积物不稳定。

examples.en: Chemists analysed marine sediment for traces of ancient pollution.
examples.cn: 化学家分析海洋沉积物中的古代污染痕迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: marine（海的）+ sediment（沉降物）＝海底沉下来的东西；陆上碎屑、生物壳、化学沉淀三路来源，一层层压成档案。

root: marine（拉丁 mare「海」→ marinus「海的」）+ sediment（拉丁 sedimentum「沉降物」，源自 sedere「坐下」）；短语为英语，成分全为拉丁语源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one settling: the whole cover, its land and biological and chemical sources, its layering, its texture, its sampling, and its behaviour as ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次沉降展开：整个覆盖层、它的陆源与生物与化学来源、它的层序、它的质地、它的采样，以及它作为地基的表现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fine particles falling through dark water and stacking into layers on the seafloor.
core.cn: 核心意象：细颗粒穿过深水落下，在海底堆成一层层。

branches.en: THE COVER AND LAND SOURCE: the whole blanket, then the eroded rock that feeds it.
branches.cn: 覆盖层与陆源：先是整张毯子，再是供养它的侵蚀碎屑。

branches.en: SHELL AND CHEMISTRY: plankton remains and precipitates join the pile.
branches.cn: 贝壳与化学：浮游生物遗骸与沉淀加入堆积。

branches.en: TIME AND TEXTURE: layers record time, grain size records flow.
branches.cn: 时间与质地：层记录时间，粒径记录流动。

branches.en: SAMPLE: what the core brings up is the same material made portable.

definition_zh: 名词：烤架；烧烤聚会；烤肉。动词：用烤架烤（肉或鱼）
definition_en: a metal frame or gas grill for cooking food over fire; an outdoor meal cooked this way; the meat itself; to cook food on such a grill
core_image: 炭火上支着一张铁架，肉在上面滋滋冒油
scene: 周末后院飘起炭火味，邻居把腌好的肉端了过来。 We lit the barbecue and waited for the coals to turn grey.
sceneCN: 这里 barbecue 是「烤架」（第 1 个义项：架在火上烤肉的器具）；句意是我们点起烤架，等炭火转成灰白。

senses.title: The grill itself
senses.definition: a metal frame or gas device for cooking food over an open fire
senses.definitionCN: 架在明火上烤食物的金属架或燃气器具
senses.example: We lit the barbecue and waited for the coals to turn grey.
senses.exampleCN: 我们点起烤架，等炭火转成灰白。
senses.why: The Taino barbacoa was a raised wooden frame; English kept the frame sense when the frame became metal.
senses.whyCN: 泰诺语 barbacoa 本指架高的木台；英语保留了「架子」这一义，只是木架换成了铁架。

senses.title: The outdoor meal
senses.definition: an outdoor party where food is cooked and eaten over a fire
senses.definitionCN: 在户外生火烤肉并一起吃的聚会
senses.example: They invited us to a backyard barbecue on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们邀我们周日去后院烧烤。
senses.why: Cooking a whole animal outdoors became a social event, so the apparatus lent its name to the gathering.
senses.whyCN: 在户外烤整只牲畜成了社交活动，于是器具之名转指聚会本身。

senses.title: The meat on the plate
senses.definition: meat, especially pork or beef, slow-cooked over smoke in the American South
senses.definitionCN: 肉，尤指美国南部以烟慢烤的猪肉或牛肉
senses.example: The barbecue was tender enough to pull apart with a fork.
senses.exampleCN: 这份烤肉嫩得能用叉子撕开。
senses.why: In the American South the word narrowed from the event to the smoked meat served at it.
senses.whyCN: 在美国南部，词义从「聚会」收窄为席上那块烟熏肉。

senses.title: To cook on the grill
senses.definition: to cook meat or fish over an open fire or hot coals
senses.definitionCN: 在明火或热炭上烤（肉或鱼）
senses.example: She barbecued the chicken with a honey glaze.
senses.exampleCN: 她给鸡刷上蜂蜜汁再烤。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb with no added ending, as English often does with cooking words.
senses.whyCN: 名词不加词尾直接转为动词，这是英语烹饪词的常见做法。

senses.title: The Australian barbie
senses.definition: in Australian and New Zealand speech, a clipped form naming the outdoor grill
senses.definitionCN: 澳新口语中的缩略说法，指户外烤炉
senses.example: Put another steak on the barbie before the rain starts.
senses.exampleCN: 趁雨还没下，再往烤炉上放块牛排。
senses.why: Australian English clips long words and adds -ie, giving barbie from barbecue.
senses.whyCN: 澳洲英语爱把长词截短再加 -ie，barbecue 于是成了 barbie。

intro.en: Barbecue began as a Caribbean wooden frame and ended as a backyard party.
intro.cn: barbecue 起于加勒比的一张木架，终于后院的一场聚会。

items.en: Taino speakers in the Caribbean used barbacoa for a raised wooden frame that smoked or dried meat.
items.cn: 加勒比泰诺人用 barbacoa 指一种架高的木台，用来熏肉或晾干肉。

items.en: Spanish took the word as barbacoa; Oviedo recorded it in his account of the Indies in 1526.
items.cn: 西班牙语借入为 barbacoa；奥维耶多在 1526 年的西印度群岛记述中已记录此词。

items.en: English borrowed it as barbecue, first for the frame and then for a whole animal roasted on it.
items.cn: 英语借入为 barbecue，先指木架，再指架上烤的整只牲畜。

items.en: Pit-cooking whole hogs outdoors turned the word into a regional food and a social event.
items.cn: 美国南部露天坑烤整猪，使这个词变成一种地方食物与一场社交活动。

items.en: Australian and New Zealand English clipped it to barbie for the backyard grill.
items.cn: 澳新英语把它截短为 barbie，专指后院烤炉。

items.en: Today barbecue is a noun, a verb and the name of the grill itself.
items.cn: 今天 barbecue 既是名词、动词，也是烤炉本身的名字。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bar- opening; the near-meaning group gives other words for cooking over fire.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bar- 开头；近义组是其他「明火烹饪」的词。

definition_zh: v. 有益于；起作用；（用于反身句式）利用；n. 效用；益处（多见于固定短语）
definition_en: To be of use or help; reflexively, to make use of an offer or chance; as a noun, use or benefit, now mainly in set phrases.
core_image: 手里那点力气到底顶不顶用
scene: 律师劝他利用这次免费复核的机会。 The lawyer urged him to avail himself of the free review.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：avail oneself of 表示利用某个机会或条件，是这个词最常见的现代用法。

senses.title: To be of use
senses.definition: to help or produce a useful effect, often used in the negative
senses.definitionCN: 有所帮助或产生有用的效果，常用于否定句
senses.example: Protests availed nothing against the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议对该决定毫无作用。
senses.why: Avail joins a-, to, with val, worth, so it literally means to be worth something to someone.
senses.whyCN: avail 由 a-「向」与 val「价值」构成，字面就是「对某人有价值」。

senses.title: To make use of
senses.definition: in the reflexive pattern avail oneself of, to take advantage of an offer, chance or facility
senses.definitionCN: 用于反身句式，指利用某个机会、条件或设施
senses.example: Few residents availed themselves of the grant.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有居民利用这项补助。
senses.why: If something is worth something to you, you can turn that worth to account, which is exactly what the reflexive pattern says.
senses.whyCN: 既然某物对你有价值，你就可以把这份价值用起来，这正是反身句式所表达的意思。

senses.title: Use or benefit
senses.definition: as a noun, help or advantage, surviving chiefly in set phrases of little use
senses.definitionCN: 作名词指帮助或好处，主要保留在表示收效甚微的固定短语中
senses.example: All their pleading was of no avail.
senses.exampleCN: 他们所有的恳求都毫无用处。
senses.why: The noun kept the old sense of worth, and because it froze inside set phrases it now sounds formal.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「价值」这一旧义，又因固定在短语内部，如今听起来偏正式。

intro.en: Avail is a- plus vail, from Old French valoir, to be worth, from Latin valere, to be strong or worth; the same root gives value and valid.
intro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail，出自古法语 valoir「有价值」，源自拉丁语 valere「强健、有价值」；同一词根产生 value 与 valid。

items.en: A root meaning to be strong lies behind words of worth, health and power.
items.cn: 一个表示「强健」的词根支撑着价值、健康与力量类的词。

items.en: Latin valere meant to be strong, to be well, and hence to be worth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为「强健、安好」，进而指「有价值」。

items.en: Old French valoir kept the sense of being worth a price or a benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 valoir 保留了「值某个价钱或有某种好处」的意思。

items.en: With a-, to, added, avaloir meant to be of profit to someone.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 avaloir，意为「对某人有益」。

items.en: Middle English availen meant to help or profit, both as verb and noun.
items.cn: 中古英语 availen 意为「有益、有帮助」，动词名词皆可。

items.en: The bare verb faded, leaving the reflexive pattern and phrases meaning in vain.
items.cn: 单独的动词用法衰退，留下反身句式与表示徒劳的短语。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the val family and two words of similar sound; the near-meaning group lists plainer words for being of use.
note.cn: 形近组保留 val 词族和两个读音相近的词；近义组列出表示「有用」的更平易的词。
