abstract.cn: 想象对着不理你的风喊话。

examples.en: She availed herself of the shuttle bus.
examples.cn: 她利用了那趟班车。

examples.en: Their warnings availed little.
examples.cn: 他们的警告收效甚微。

examples.en: He argued for an hour, to no avail.
examples.cn: 他争了一小时，徒劳无功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ vail（与 value 同族，「价值」）——对你有价值就是 avail「有用」，把这份价值用起来就是「利用」。

root: 拉丁语 valere「强健、有价值」经古法语 valoir 加 a-「向」成 avaloir「对……有益」，入中古英语作 availen；现代主要保留反身句式与表示徒劳的固定短语。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses turn on worth: something being worth something to you, your turning that worth to use, and the worth itself named as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都围绕「价值」：某物对你有价值、你把这份价值用起来，以及把这份价值本身当名词来称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: whether the strength in your hand actually counts for anything
core.cn: 核心意象：手里那点力气到底顶不顶用

branches.en: Warnings that changed nothing.
branches.cn: 毫无作用的警告。

branches.en: Protests that failed against a decision.
branches.cn: 对决定无效的抗议。

branches.en: A resident taking up a grant.
branches.cn: 申领补助的居民。

branches.en: Pleading that was of no use.
branches.cn: 毫无用处的恳求。

branches.en: Both measure how much the effort was worth.
branches.cn: 两者都在衡量这份努力值多少。

intro.en: Avail is a- plus vail; the val root builds value, valid, prevail and equivalent.
intro.cn: avail 是 a- 加 vail；val 词根构成 value、valid、prevail 与 equivalent。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is valere, to be strong, and valor, worth; the -able ending turns it into available.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 valere「强健」与 valor「价值」；加上 -able 词尾便成 available。

definition_zh: 热衷者；狂热爱好者；笃信者
definition_en: a person who is extremely interested in and active about a subject or activity
core_image: 展览馆里一个人围着同一件展品转了三圈，逢人便讲它的来历
scene: 每到观星季，他都在山顶守着望远镜到天亮。 He is an enthusiast of amateur astronomy.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiast 是「狂热爱好者」（第 1 个义项：对某活动极有兴趣并投入其中的人）；句意：他是业余天文爱好者。

senses.title: A person devoted to an activity
senses.definition: someone who spends time and energy on a hobby or subject because they love it
senses.definitionCN: 因喜爱而在某项爱好或主题上投入时间与精力的人
senses.example: Local enthusiasts restored the old railway.
senses.exampleCN: 当地爱好者修复了这条老铁路。
senses.why: The word first named a person filled with divine inspiration, so the modern hobbyist keeps that sense of being possessed by an interest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指被神灵灵感充满的人，因此今天的爱好者仍保留被兴趣占据的意味。

senses.title: An active supporter of a cause
senses.definition: a person who works eagerly for a political or social idea
senses.definitionCN: 热切投身某种政治或社会理念的人
senses.example: The campaign relied on committed enthusiasts.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动依靠坚定的积极分子。
senses.why: Moved from hobby to cause, the noun stresses belief and effort rather than pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 从爱好转向事业后，这个名词强调信念与投入，而非乐趣。

senses.title: A person claimed to be inspired from above
senses.titleCN: 灵恩狂信者（历史宗教义）
senses.definition: in older religious writing, someone who professed direct inspiration by a deity
senses.definitionCN: 在早期宗教文献中指声称受神灵直接启示的人
senses.example: Critics dismissed the preacher as an enthusiast.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这位布道者为狂信者。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: god within, a person moved by a power they cannot control.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：神明在内，人被自身无法控制的力量推动。

intro.en: Enthusiast literally means having a god within, from Greek en and theos.
intro.cn: enthusiast 字面义是内有神明，来自希腊语 en 与 theos。

items.en: En theos means with a god or inspired.
items.cn: en theos 意为有神附身、受启示。

items.en: Enthousiasmos named the state of being possessed.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 指被神灵附体的状态。

items.en: Entusiasmus carries the term into learned Latin.
items.cn: entusiasmus 是该词的拉丁写法。

items.en: Enthousiaste gives the English its modern shape.
items.cn: enthousiaste 为英语提供现代词形。

items.en: English uses it as a criticism of religious excess.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用以批评宗教狂热。

items.en: The word softens into the neutral hobbyist sense.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词淡化，成为中性的爱好者义。

note.en: Group one holds the family built on the same stem; group two holds other words for keen people.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干的同族词；第二组是其他指热心者的词。

entries.definition: The emotion itself, while the person noun names someone moved by it.
entries.definitionCN: 指情感本身，而指人的词表示被这种情感驱动者。

entries.definition: The adjective of the same family, far more common in daily speech.
entries.definitionCN: 同族形容词，日常口语远比名词常用。

entries.definition: Built on the same Greek word for god, but it names a belief rather than a temper.
entries.definitionCN: 同样基于表神的希腊语，但指信仰而非性情。

entries.definition: A doctrinal label sharing the same person suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 共享同一人物词尾的教义标签。

entries.definition: Someone devoted to a person or cause, with loyalty rather than energy stressed.
entries.definitionCN: 忠于某人或某事者，强调忠诚而非热情。

entries.definition: An enthusiastic amateur with real knowledge, as in a history buff.
entries.definitionCN: 懂行的热心业余者，如历史迷。

entries.definition: A Spanish borrowing for a devoted fan of a defined field.
entries.definitionCN: 借自西班牙语，指某领域的忠实爱好者。

entries.definition: Much stronger and mostly negative: someone uncompromising in a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 语气强得多且多为贬义，指狂热党派者。

normalIntro.en: Split enthusiast into en plus theia, a god, so the person originally had a god inside.
normalIntro.cn: 把 enthusiast 拆成 en 与 theia（神），因此这人原本内有神明。

normal.en: The person is an enthusiast; the feeling is enthusiasm.
normal.cn: 人叫 enthusiast，情感叫 enthusiasm。

normal.en: Say enthusiast for something, rarely for somebody.
normal.cn: 常说某事的 enthusiast，很少说某人的。

normal.en: In reviews it is a compliment; in older religious texts it was an accusation.
normal.cn: 在评论中它是褒义，在旧宗教文献中却是指责。

normal.en: The adjective enthusiastic is neutral and safe in essays.
normal.cn: 形容词 enthusiastic 中性，写作可放心使用。

normal.en: Countable noun: two enthusiasts, not two enthusiasm.
normal.cn: 可数名词：two enthusiasts，不是 two enthusiasm。

abstract.en: Picture a visitor who cannot leave a single exhibit.
abstract.cn: 想象一位在一件展品前舍不得离开的观众。

abstract.en: Imagine a lantern carried through the town long after the festival ends.
abstract.cn: 想象节日结束后仍在城中提着灯笼的人。

abstract.en: Think of a trembling figure said to speak with a voice not its own.
abstract.cn: 想想古人所说颤抖着、以非自身声音说话的人。

examples.en: He became an enthusiast for urban cycling.
examples.cn: 他成了城市骑行的热心者。

examples.en: Car enthusiasts meet at the depot each Sunday.
examples.cn: 车迷每个周日在车库集合。

examples.en: She is a keen enthusiast of silent films.
examples.cn: 她是默片的忠实爱好者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因谁求济事」——因为谁来都急着帮忙做事，所以 enthusiast 是热心者；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 en（在内）＋ theos（神）→ enthousios（有神附身）→ enthousiasmos → 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 法语 enthousiaste → 英语 enthusiast，核心义「内心被点燃的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun runs from religious possession to eager support of a cause and finally to the ordinary hobbyist.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从宗教性的神灵附体，走向对事业的热切支持，最后落到日常的爱好者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire lit inside a person that shows in everything they do.
core.cn: 核心意象：人内心燃起的火，显现在他做的一切之中。

branches.en: Ordinary devotion to a hobby is the modern core.
branches.cn: 对爱好的投入是现代核心用法。

branches.en: Causes borrow the same energy in a public form.
branches.cn: 事业以公共形式借用同一种能量。

branches.en: The oldest sense still appears in histories of religion.
branches.cn: 最古义项仍见于宗教史著作。

branches.en: Both describe someone ruled by an inner impulse.
branches.cn: 两者都描述被内在冲动支配的人。

branches.en: Conviction links the campaigner to the inspired preacher.
branches.cn: 信念把运动者与受启示的布道者相连。

intro.en: A Greek compound of with plus god is extended by English person and quality endings.
intro.cn: 希腊语「神在内」的复合词由英语人物与性质词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin Deus and Greek Theos both name god, and both feed English words such as deism and theology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 deus 与希腊语 theos 都表神，分别进入 deism 与 theology 等英语词。

items.exampleCN: en- 位于希腊复合词开头。

items.example: The adjective is the direct ancestor.

definition_en: a published collection of chosen writings, such as poems or stories, often by different authors
core_image: 一束采下的花，被扎成花环
scene: 书店橱窗里摆着新出的诗集，书脊一排颜色雅致。 Her poem was chosen for the school's annual anthology of student writing.
sceneCN: 这里 anthology 是「选集」（第 1 个义项：选取的作品合集）；句意为她的诗被选入学校年度学生作品选。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「选集编者」
由本词加 -ical 构成，义为「选集的」

senses.title: A collection of literary works
senses.definition: a book collecting selected poems, stories, or essays, often by several writers
senses.definitionCN: 收录精选诗歌、小说或散文的书，常出自多位作者
senses.example: The anthology gathers a century of American short stories.
senses.exampleCN: 这部选集汇集了美国百年短篇小说。
senses.why: Greek anthos 'flower' plus logia 'gathering' made a 'garland of flowers'; chosen poems are the flowers, the book is the garland.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anthos「花」加 logia「收集」构成「花环」；被选的诗是花，书是花环。

senses.title: A collection of similar things in any field
senses.definition: a set of representative examples gathered from a field, such as music, film, or jokes
senses.definitionCN: 从某一领域汇集的代表性例子，如音乐、影视或笑话
senses.example: The band released an anthology of their best recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队发行了精选录音合集。
senses.why: Once the garland picture existed, any field could pick its best blooms and bind them together.
senses.whyCN: 花环的意象一旦成立，任何领域都可以摘取最美的花并扎成一束。

intro.en: Anthology comes from Greek anthologia, 'a gathering of flowers', later 'a garland of poems'.
intro.cn: anthology 来自希腊语 anthologia「花的集合」，后指「诗的花环」。

items.en: The root *andh- meant 'to bloom', also behind anther, the pollen-bearing part of a flower.
items.cn: 词根 *andh- 意为「开花」，也见于 anther「花药」。

items.en: Anthos meant 'flower'; it survives in chrysanthemum, the golden flower.
items.cn: anthos 意为「花」；保留在 chrysanthemum「金色的花，菊花」中。

items.en: Meleager and later scholars titled their poem collections anthologia, a garland of chosen verses.
items.cn: 墨勒阿格罗斯及后世学者把诗集题作 anthologia，即精选诗篇的花环。

items.era: GREEK TO LATIN TO ENGLISH, 17TH C.
items.en: The word passed through Latin into English in the seventeenth century, first for Greek poem collections.
items.cn: 该词经拉丁语于十七世纪进入英语，最初指希腊诗集。

items.en: Modern use extends to music, film, and even television anthology series.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展到音乐、电影，乃至单元剧形式的选集式剧集。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers anthos-family words and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers collection words.
note.cn: 形近组收 anthos 词族与拼形相近词；近义组收「合集」类词。

entries.definition: The golden-flower plant; shares anthos, the Greek flower word.
entries.definitionCN: 菊花；共享希腊语 anthos「花」。

entries.definition: The pollen-bearing part of a flower's stamen; same anthos root.
entries.definitionCN: 花药，雄蕊的载粉部分；同 anthos 词根。

entries.definition: The study of humans; starts similarly but the root is anthropos 'human', not flower.
entries.definitionCN: 人类学；开头相近，但词根是 anthropos「人」，并非「花」。

entries.definition: A general word for gathered items, chosen or not.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指收集之物，不强调精选。

entries.definition: A condensed collection of knowledge on a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「概要；汇编」，偏重知识浓缩。

entries.definition: A volume containing several works by one author.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「合集本」，多收同一作者的多部作品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the flower root anthos, the garland image, and the -logy gathering ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用词根 anthos「花」、花环意象，以及表「收集」的 -logy 词尾。

normal.en: anthos + logia: a gathering of flowers, a garland of poems.
normal.cn: anthos 加 logia：花的集合，诗的花环。

normal.en: Chrysanthemum shares the flower root: golden flower.
normal.cn: chrysanthemum 共享花词根：金色的花。

normal.en: The Greek Anthology is the famous ancient poem garland.
normal.cn: 《希腊选集》是著名的古代诗歌花环。

normal.en: Anthropology starts the same but studies humans, not flowers.
normal.cn: anthropology 开头相同，但研究的是人而非花。

normal.en: The plural keeps the -y: two anthologies.
normal.cn: 复数保持 -y 变化：两本 anthologies。

abstract.en: Picture wildflowers picked one by one and tied into a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象野花被一朵朵采下并扎成一环。

abstract.en: Picture a bookshelf where each book is a vase of chosen blooms.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上每本书都是一瓶精选的花。

abstract.en: Picture a playlist titled best of, built like a bouquet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张名为「精选」的歌单，像花束一样编成。

examples.en: She read the whole anthology in two evenings.
examples.cn: 她两个晚上就读完了整部选集。

examples.en: The museum published an anthology of artists' letters.
examples.cn: 博物馆出版了艺术家书信选。

examples.en: Each episode of the anthology series tells a new story.
examples.cn: 这部单元剧的每一集都讲一个新故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安搜集」——安安静静把好文章搜集起来，就是「选集」

root: 希腊语 anthos（花）+ logia（收集）→ anthologia（花环；诗选）→ 英语 anthology；核心意象是「把最好的花扎成一束」。

sensesIntro.en: From the literary garland the sense widens to any curated set of best examples.
sensesIntro.cn: 由文学花环扩展到任何领域的精选合集。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a garland woven from the best flowers picked in the field
core.cn: 核心意象：用野外采下的最好的花编成的花环

branches.en: The literature line: poems and stories bound like flowers.
branches.cn: 文学线：诗歌与小说像花一样被扎成一册。

branches.en: The field line: music, film, or jokes get their own garland.
branches.cn: 领域线：音乐、影视或笑话也各有自己的花环。

branches.en: Both require choice: only the picked blooms enter.
branches.cn: 两者都要求挑选：只有被选中的花才入册。

branches.en: The editor is the gardener who decides which flowers stay.
branches.cn: 编者是园丁，决定哪些花留下。

branches.en: The word now names even an anthology series on television.
branches.cn: 如今该词甚至用于电视上的选集式剧集。

intro.en: The word joins the Greek root anthos 'flower' with -logy, a gathering or study.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊词根 anthos「花」与表示「收集、研究」的 -logy 相连。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family; the entries record the Greek source words.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁词族；条目记录希腊语源头词。

items.example: It supplies the flower in anthology.
items.exampleCN: 它为 anthology 提供花义。

items.example: It forms anthologist, the editor of a collection.
Anthropos means human, a different root.
items.exampleCN: anthropos 意为人，是另一个词根。

items.example: It appears in podium and stadium.

definition_zh: 问卷；调查表；问题清单；（研究用的）问卷工具
definition_en: a printed or digital set of questions used to collect information from a group of people
core_image: 一叠同样的问题发给很多人，回来的纸上写满勾选
scene: 这里指「问卷」。 Only half of the patients returned the follow-up questionnaire on sleep quality.
sceneCN: 这里 questionnaire 是「问卷」（第 1 个义项：一组书面问题构成的调查表）；句意：只有一半病人交回了关于睡眠质量的随访问卷。图中可辨识物件：同一叠表格、勾选方框、回邮信封。

senses.title: A set of written questions
senses.definition: a printed or digital form containing a series of questions for many respondents
senses.definitionCN: 含一系列问题、供众多受访者使用的印刷或电子表格
senses.example: The clinic hands every new patient a short health questionnaire.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所给每位新病人一份简短的健康问卷。
senses.why: The defining feature is sameness: one set of questions is given to many people, so the answers can later be lined up side by side.
senses.whyCN: 决定性特征是相同：同一组问题给许多人，好让回答后来可以并排对齐。

senses.title: A research instrument
senses.definition: a standardised tool used by researchers to collect comparable answers across a sample
senses.definitionCN: 研究者用来在样本中收集可比回答的标准化工具
senses.example: The team validated the questionnaire before sending it to two thousand households.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在对两千户发放前先验证了这份问卷。
senses.why: Research turned the form into an instrument: the same wording is given to everyone so that answers can be counted and compared.
senses.whyCN: 研究把表格变成工具：同一套措辞给所有人，好让回答能被计数与比较。

senses.title: A clinical self-report
senses.definition: a standard set of questions on which a patient reports symptoms, mood or function
senses.definitionCN: 由病人自报症状、情绪或功能的一套标准问题
senses.example: The depression questionnaire asks about the past two weeks only.
senses.exampleCN: 这份抑郁自评问卷只询问过去两周的情况。
senses.why: Clinical use narrows the set to symptoms and a fixed time window, so that scores from different patients mean the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法把问题集合收窄到症状与固定时间窗，使不同病人的分数含义相同。

senses.title: A survey by post or link
senses.titleCN: 通过邮寄或链接进行的调查
senses.definition: the whole exercise of distributing forms and collecting completed answers
senses.definitionCN: 分发表格并收集已填回答的整个活动
senses.example: Response rates to the postal questionnaire were lower than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 邮寄问卷的回收率低于预期。
senses.why: The word can name the operation, not just the paper: a questionnaire is also the round of asking and collecting that the form makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能指整个操作而非仅指纸张：问卷也是这张表所促成的询问与回收轮次。

senses.title: A hiring or admissions form
senses.titleCN: 招聘或入学的问题清单
senses.definition: a list of questions used by an employer or school to screen applicants
senses.definitionCN: 雇主或学校用来筛选申请者的问题清单
senses.example: The application questionnaire asked candidates to describe a difficult decision.
senses.exampleCN: 申请问卷要求候选人描述一次艰难的决定。
senses.why: Screening is a different purpose for the same instrument: identical questions let a hundred applicants be judged against one standard.
senses.whyCN: 筛选是同一工具的另一种用途：相同的问题让上百名申请者按同一标准被评判。

senses.title: An online form
senses.definition: a digital questionnaire delivered by web link or app, often with automatic scoring
senses.definitionCN: 通过网络链接或应用发放、常带自动计分的电子问卷
senses.example: The online questionnaire closed automatically after five hundred replies.
senses.exampleCN: 在线问卷在收到五百份回复后自动关闭。
senses.why: The delivery method changed, the instrument did not: the same questions travel by link and return already encoded as data.
senses.whyCN: 投递方式变了，工具没变：同样的问题通过链接发送，回来时已编码成数据。

senses.title: A structured interview schedule
senses.definition: a fixed list of questions read aloud in the same order to every interviewee
senses.definitionCN: 按同一顺序向每位受访者念出的固定问题清单
senses.example: Interviewers read the questionnaire aloud and recorded answers verbatim.
senses.exampleCN: 访谈员朗读问卷并逐字记录回答。
senses.why: Reading aloud keeps the wording identical from one respondent to the next, which is what makes the answers comparable at all.
senses.whyCN: 朗读使措辞在每位受访者之间保持完全一致，这正是回答得以比较的前提。

senses.title: A statistical data source
senses.definition: the instrument whose answers become variables in a statistical analysis
senses.definitionCN: 其回答将成为统计分析变量的工具
senses.example: Income data in the study came from a household questionnaire.
senses.exampleCN: 研究中的收入数据来自一份家庭问卷。
senses.why: Once answers are coded, the sheet becomes a column in a data set: that is how a paper instrument turns into statistical evidence.
senses.whyCN: 回答一经编码，表格就成为数据集中的一列：纸质工具正是这样变成统计证据。

intro.en: Questionnaire is a French word, built from question plus the suffix -aire, which comes from Latin -arius. Question itself goes back to Latin quaestio and quaerere, 'to seek or ask'. English borrowed the French form in the 19th century, when social surveys began to need a name for the printed list.
intro.cn: questionnaire 是法语词，由 question 加后缀 -aire 构成，后者来自拉丁 -arius。question 本身可回溯到拉丁 quaestio 与 quaerere“寻求、询问”。英语在 19 世纪借入法语形式，当时社会调查开始需要为印刷问题清单起名。

items.en: Quaerere meant 'to seek, to ask, to inquire'. It is the verb behind question, query, inquiry, require and acquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为“寻求、询问、探究”，是 question、query、inquiry、require、acquire 背后的动词。

items.en: Quaestio named a seeking or an inquiry, and in legal use an investigation. French turned it into question.
items.cn: quaestio 命名寻求或探究，法律上指调查。法语把它变成 question。

items.en: French question kept both the asking and the doubting senses, and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 法语 question 同时保留“询问”与“质疑”两义，英语在中世纪借入。

items.en: The French suffix -aire, from Latin -arius, marks a person or thing connected with something, as in bibliothécaire or questionnaire.
items.cn: 法语后缀 -aire 来自拉丁 -arius，标记与某物相关的人或物，如 bibliothécaire 与 questionnaire。

items.en: French formed questionnaire in the 19th century for a set of questions used in an inquiry. English adopted the spelling unchanged.
items.cn: 法语在 19 世纪造出 questionnaire，指调查中使用的一组问题。英语原样采用了这个拼写。

items.en: Sample surveys, market research and clinical scales made the questionnaire a standard instrument with rules for design and validation.
items.cn: 抽样调查、市场研究与临床量表使问卷成为有设计与验证规范的标准工具。

note.en: The look-alike group separates questionnaire from question, questioner and the similar-looking but different-root quest. The meaning group compares surveys, polls and forms.
note.cn: 形近组区分 questionnaire 与 question、questioner，以及拼写相近但词根不同的 quest；词义组比较调查、民意测验与表格。

entries.definition: a single inquiry, or to ask. It is the base word, while questionnaire names a whole set.
entries.definitionCN: 单个问题，或询问。它是基础词，而 questionnaire 命名整套问题。

entries.definition: a person who asks questions. It names the asker, not the paper.
entries.definitionCN: 提出问题的人。它命名提问者，而不是纸张。

entries.definition: doubtful or open to suspicion. It shares the root but moves toward doubt rather than inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 可疑的、有问题的。它共享词根，但转向怀疑而非询问。

entries.definition: a long search or journey. It comes from the same seeking verb but names a search, not a form.
entries.definitionCN: 漫长的寻找或旅程。它来自同一个“寻求”动词，却命名寻找，而非表格。

entries.definition: the whole research exercise of collecting data from a sample. The questionnaire is only its instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 从样本收集数据的整个研究活动。问卷只是它的工具。

entries.definition: a count of opinions, usually political. It is a short survey, often with one or two questions.
entries.definitionCN: 意见计数，通常指政治民调。它是简短调查，常只有一两个问题。

entries.definition: a document with blanks to complete. It collects facts, while a questionnaire collects answers to questions.
entries.definitionCN: 留有空白待填的文件。它收集事实，而问卷收集对问题的回答。

entries.definition: a standard list of items or symptoms to be checked. In clinical use it is close to a questionnaire.
entries.definitionCN: 供勾选的标准条目或症状清单。在临床用法中接近问卷。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of one stack of identical questions, then let it cover research, clinics, post, hiring, online forms, interviews and statistics.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩保留“一叠完全相同的问题”的画面，再让它覆盖研究、诊所、邮寄、招聘、线上表格、访谈与统计。

normal.en: Split it as question + aire: question + French noun ending. It is a set of questions wearing a French coat.
normal.cn: 拆成 question + aire：问题、法语名词词尾。它是一组问题披着法语的衣裳。

normal.en: Picture one stack of identical sheets handed to a whole room.
normal.cn: 想象一叠完全相同的表格发给整个房间的人。

normal.en: The returned sheets are what makes it research: same questions, comparable answers.
normal.cn: 收回的表格才使它成为研究：同样的问题，可比的回答。

normal.en: Tear one sheet off the stack and you have a form; keep the stack and you have a survey.
normal.cn: 从一叠里撕下一张，你得到表格；保留整叠，你得到调查。

normal.en: In a clinic the stack asks about symptoms; in an office it asks about decisions.
normal.cn: 在诊所，这一叠问症状；在办公室，这一叠问决策。

abstract.en: Notice that the noun names the instrument, not the finding: the results belong to the survey, not to the paper.
abstract.cn: 注意这个名词命名工具，而非发现：结果属于调查，而不属于纸张。

abstract.en: Keep the -aire ending visible: it is a French borrowing, so the spelling has no English -er.
abstract.cn: 让 -aire 词尾保持可见：它是法语借词，因此拼写里没有英语的 -er。

abstract.en: Remember the pair: a questionnaire is answered by respondents, an interview schedule is read by an interviewer.
abstract.cn: 记住配对：问卷由受访者填写，访谈问题表由访谈员朗读。

examples.en: Every participant completed a questionnaire on diet and exercise.
examples.cn: 每位参与者都填写了一份饮食与运动问卷。

examples.en: The questionnaire was translated into three languages before the survey began.
examples.cn: 调查开始前，问卷被译成三种语言。

examples.en: Researchers piloted the questionnaire on forty students to catch unclear wording.
examples.cn: 研究者先在四十名学生中试用问卷，以发现含糊的措辞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“快身耐儿”：快把身上耐性勾一勾，一张问卷问到底。

root: 法语 questionnaire（19 世纪），由 question 加 -aire（源自拉丁 -arius）构成；question 出自拉丁 quaestio、quaerere“寻求、询问”。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense is a set of identical questions: printed for a clinic, standardised for research, self-reported in medicine, mailed or linked, used to screen applicants, read aloud in interviews, and coded into statistical variables. The paper changes form; the sameness of the questions does not.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是一组完全相同的问题：为诊所印制、为研究标准化、在医学中自评、通过邮寄或链接发放、用来筛选申请者、在访谈中朗读，并被编码成统计变量。纸张的形式在变，问题的同一性不变。

core.en: One set of questions is repeated for many people so that the answers can be compared.
core.cn: 同一组问题被重复给许多人，好让回答可以比较。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a standard set of questions serves research.
branches.cn: 工具：一套标准问题服务研究。

branches.en: DATA: clinical reports and coded answers become variables.
branches.cn: 数据：临床报告与被编码的回答变成变量。

branches.en: DELIVERY: post and web links carry the same sheets outward.
branches.cn: 发放：邮寄与网络链接把同样的表格送出去。

branches.en: SCREENING: employers and schools use the list to judge applicants.
branches.cn: 筛选：雇主与学校用这份清单判断申请者。

branches.en: INTERVIEW: an interviewer reads the fixed list aloud in order.
branches.cn: 访谈：访谈员按顺序朗读固定清单。

intro.en: Questionnaire is question plus the French suffix -aire. The items below follow the asking verb through its person, adjective and the seeking relatives.
intro.cn: questionnaire 由 question 与法语后缀 -aire 构成。下列条目沿着“询问”动词，走过人称、形容词以及“寻求”亲属词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the seeking verb and the inquiry noun. They explain why question, query, require and acquire all belong to one family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“寻求”动词与“探究”名词，解释为什么 question、query、require 与 acquire 同属一个词族。

items.meaning: a set of questions for many respondents
items.exampleCN: 这份问卷有二十个题目。

items.meaning: an inquiry; to ask or doubt
items.exampleCN: 有一个问题仍未得到回答。

items.example: The questioner raised her hand again.

items.meaning: the act of asking; showing doubt

items.example: She sent a query about the invoice.

items.meaning: to seek again, hence to demand
to seek toward oneself, hence to obtain
items.example: The museum acquired the painting in 1960.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆于 1960 年获得这幅画。

definition_zh: 结果、因此；由于前面所说的情况，后面出现这样的后果（作衔接状语）
definition_en: because of what has just been stated; consequently
core_image: 一排骨牌依次倒下，最后一块压住了地上的纸
scene: 仓库的通风口被纸箱堵住，温度一夜之间升高，冷藏的货物开始变质。 As a result, half of the shipment had to be thrown away.
sceneCN: 这里取「结果、因此」（第 1 个义项：在句首承接前因、引出后果）；句意为结果有一半货物不得不丢弃。

senses.title: The connector at the front
senses.definition: used at the beginning of a sentence to introduce the consequence of what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 用在句首，引出刚才所述情况带来的后果
senses.example: The pipe froze, and as a result the whole floor was flooded.
senses.exampleCN: 管子冻住了，结果整层楼都被水淹了。
senses.why: Result began as a springing back, and a consequence is what bounces out of an earlier event.
senses.whyCN: 结果本指弹回，后果正是从先前事件中弹出来的东西。

senses.title: Why it takes no cause
senses.titleCN: 结构边界：本身不接原因
senses.definition: the bare phrase states the effect only; the version with of is needed to name the cause
senses.definitionCN: 光用这个短语只陈述结果；要说出原因，必须用带上该介词的形式
senses.example: As a result of the delay, the opening was moved to autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 由于这次延误，开幕改到了秋天。
senses.why: English splits the job: one form points forward to the effect, the other backward to the cause.
senses.whyCN: 英语把功能分开：一种形式指向后果，另一种回指原因。

senses.title: Register beside a single adverb
senses.titleCN: 语域义：与单词副词的分工
senses.definition: it is the fuller, more explicit choice, while a single adverb such as consequently is tighter and more formal
senses.definitionCN: 它是更完整、更明白的选择，而单个副词更紧凑、更正式
senses.example: The sample was too small; as a result, the finding is weak.
senses.exampleCN: 样本太小，因此结论不够有力。
senses.why: A two-word frame slows the reader down at the hinge of an argument.
senses.whyCN: 由两个词构成的框架会让读者在论证的铰接处放慢速度。

senses.title: Effect versus inference
senses.titleCN: 辨义：事实结果不同于逻辑推导
senses.definition: it marks what actually followed, while an inference word marks what must be concluded
senses.definitionCN: 它标出实际随之发生的事，而推论词标出必然得出的判断
senses.example: He missed the deadline and as a result lost the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 他误了期限，结果丢掉了合同。
senses.why: A result is an event in the world; an inference is a move in an argument.
senses.whyCN: 结果是世上发生的事，推论是论证中的一步。

senses.title: Mid-sentence and final position
senses.definition: it can close a clause as well as open a sentence, so the effect may come after the cause and then be labelled
senses.definitionCN: 它既可开启句子，也可收束分句，因此后果可以先出现、再被标注
senses.example: The filter clogged and the pump failed as a result.
senses.exampleCN: 滤芯堵了，水泵因此失灵。
senses.why: Placing the frame last makes the causal link feel discovered rather than announced.
senses.whyCN: 把框架放在最后，因果关系像是被发现的，而不是被宣告的。

senses.title: The report habit
senses.titleCN: 学术义：报告与论文中的衔接
senses.definition: in reports and papers it links a finding to its practical consequence without adding interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 在报告与论文中，把一项发现与其实际后果连接起来，不添加解释
senses.example: Two variables were uncontrolled, and as a result the comparison is limited.
senses.exampleCN: 有两个变量未受控，因此比较的结论有限。
senses.why: Research writing needs neutral connectors, and this one states causation without assigning blame.
senses.whyCN: 研究写作需要中性衔接语，这个说法陈述因果而不归咎。

senses.title: Fact, not purpose
senses.definition: it reports what happened because of an earlier event, not what someone intended to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 它陈述因先前事件而发生的事，而非某人打算达成的事
senses.example: The firm cut staff, and as a result output fell.
senses.exampleCN: 公司裁减员工，结果产量下降。
senses.why: Cause and purpose point in opposite directions in time: one looks back, the other forward.
senses.whyCN: 原因与目的在时间上指向相反：一个回望，一个前瞻。

senses.title: The spoken summary
senses.titleCN: 口语义：日常叙事中的收束
senses.definition: in speech it often sums up a chain of small events with a single consequence
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中，常用一个后果来收束一连串小事
senses.example: We left late, and as a result we missed the train.
senses.exampleCN: 我们出门晚了，结果错过了火车。
senses.why: The phrase works at any scale, from a missed train to a failed policy.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语适用于任何尺度，从错过火车到政策失败。

intro.en: Result comes from Latin resultare, to spring back, from re-, back, and saltare, to leap. The Latin chain is secure; the connector is modern English.
intro.cn: result 来自拉丁语 resultare「弹回」，由 re-「向后」与 saltare「跳」构成。拉丁语链条清楚；衔接用法是近代英语的发展。

items.en: Salire meant to leap, and its family covers jumping, assault and a range of sudden movements.
items.cn: salire 意为跳，其词族涵盖跳跃、冲击与多种突发动作。

items.en: The repeated form described leaping again and again, closer to dancing than to a single bound.
items.cn: 这个反复形式描写一再跳跃，比单次跃起更接近舞蹈。

items.en: With the prefix for back, the verb pictured something bouncing off a surface.
items.cn: 加上表向后的前缀，动词描绘某物从表面弹回。

items.en: The noun shifted from a physical rebound to whatever follows from an earlier event.
items.cn: 名词从物理弹回转为指由先前事件引出的一切。

items.en: The adverbial frame becomes common in modern expository prose; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个副词框架在近代说明文中通行，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group looks or works like a result marker but adds a cause or points elsewhere; the second group are one-word consequence words.
note.cn: 第一组外形或功能接近结果标记，但会带出原因或指向别处；第二组是单词形式的后果词。

entries.definition: It is the formal equivalent, common in reports.
entries.definitionCN: 这是正式对应说法，多用于报告。

entries.definition: It takes the cause instead of stating the effect alone.
entries.definitionCN: 它后接原因，而非只陈述结果。

entries.definition: It points forward from the cause to the effect.
entries.definitionCN: 它从原因指向结果。

entries.definition: It means after and because of an event, often of trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 意为某事之后、因其而起，常指麻烦。

entries.definition: A single word that marks the effect in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 正式文字中标记后果的单词。

entries.definition: It marks what follows logically, not necessarily what happened.
entries.definitionCN: 标出逻辑上随之而来的结论，未必是实际发生的事。

entries.definition: A short, slightly bookish marker of consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 简短、略偏书面的后果标记。

entries.definition: It can mean in this way as well as for this reason.
entries.definitionCN: 既可表如此方式，也可表因此。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real leaping and rebounding root, the real split from the cause phrase, and the real difference from inference words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的跳跃、弹回词根，与带原因形式的分工，以及和推论词的差别。

normal.en: A result rebounds: something comes back off an earlier event.
normal.cn: 结果会弹回：有东西从先前事件反弹出来。

normal.en: The bare frame points forward; the form with of points back to the cause.
normal.cn: 光用框架指向后果；带该介词的形式回指原因。

normal.en: It reports what happened, not what must be concluded.
normal.cn: 它陈述发生了什么，而非必然得出什么。

normal.en: At the end of a clause the link sounds discovered.
normal.cn: 放在分句末尾，因果关系像是被发现的。

normal.en: It works at any scale, from a missed train to a failed policy.
normal.cn: 它适用于任何尺度，从错过火车到政策失败。

abstract.en: Like dominoes falling: the last tile lands on the paper, and the fall explains it.
abstract.cn: 像骨牌接连倒下：最后一块压在纸上，倒下的过程解释了它。

abstract.en: Like a billiard ball bouncing off the cushion and hitting a second ball.
abstract.cn: 像台球从库边弹回，又撞上第二颗球。

abstract.en: Like the last domino shown in a diagram, the visible end of a chain already set in motion.
abstract.cn: 像示意图里最后那张骨牌，是一条早已启动的链条可见的末端。

examples.en: The road was closed, and as a result traffic moved inland.
examples.cn: 公路封闭，结果车流转向内陆。

examples.en: Rainfall was low; as a result, the reservoir is half empty.
examples.cn: 降雨稀少，因此水库空了一半。

examples.en: He ignored the warning, and as a result the engine seized.
examples.cn: 他忽视警告，结果发动机卡死了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿兹 阿 瑞造特」——骨牌一路倒下，最后压住那张纸：结果、因此

root: 核心名词意为结果，来自拉丁语 resultare「弹回」，由 re-「向后」与 saltare「跳」构成；由弹回引申为由某事引出的后果。该短语为近代衔接用语定型，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the sentence-opening connector, the ban on taking a cause, register beside single adverbs, effect against inference, final position, report usage, the exclusion of purpose and the spoken summary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项涵盖：句首衔接、不接原因的结构边界、与单词副词的语域分工、事实结果与逻辑推导之别、句末位置、报告用法、排除目的义，以及口语收束。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dominoes falling one after another until the last tile lands on a sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：骨牌一块接一块倒下，直到最后一块压在一张纸上。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE: the effect may be announced first or labelled after it happens.
branches.cn: 后果：既可以先宣告，也可以在发生后标注。

branches.en: THE CAUSE FORM: only the version with of can name what produced the effect.
branches.cn: 原因形式：只有带该介词的形式才能点出成因。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: reports and papers need a neutral, explicit hinge.
branches.cn: 语域：报告与论文需要一个中性、明白的铰接处。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: an event in the world differs from a step in an argument.
branches.cn: 对照：世上发生的事不同于论证中的一步。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: purpose is excluded, and everyday narration uses the same frame.
branches.cn: 边界：目的义被排除，日常叙事也用同一框架。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin noun of rebounding, so the causal link keeps a physical bounce in its history.
intro.cn: 这个短语建在一个表弹回的拉丁语名词上，因此因果联系在历史里留着一次物理弹跳。

latinIntro.en: The base verb is salire, to leap, with its repeated form saltare; resultare adds the prefix for back.
latinIntro.cn: 基础动词是 salire「跳」，其反复形式为 saltare；resultare 加上了表向后的前缀。

items.example: The verb supplies the physical core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词提供词族的物理内核。

items.example: The repeated form pictures continued motion.
items.exampleCN: 反复形式描绘持续的运动。

items.example: The prefix adds a backward direction.
English keeps both the event and the relation.

items.exampleCN: 形容词标出随之而来的东西。

items.example: The participle attaches the effect to a noun.
items.exampleCN: 分词把后果挂到名词上。

items.example: The formal twin performs the same task.
items.exampleCN: 正式同义说法承担同样功能。

items.example: Adding of turns the phrase towards the cause.
items.exampleCN: 加上该介词就把短语转向原因。

items.example: The frame is standard in modern expository prose.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架在近代说明文中是标准用法。

definition_zh: 有雄心的；野心勃勃的；规模宏大的
definition_en: having a strong desire for success or achievement; requiring great effort
core_image: 盯着山顶不肯回头望的登山者
scene: 她刚毕业就计划三年内开十家分店。 The ambitious young manager planned to open ten branch stores within three years.
sceneCN: 这里的 ambitious 是「有雄心的」（第 1 个义项：渴求成功）；句意是这位雄心勃勃的年轻经理计划三年内开出十家分店。

pos.zh: 有雄心的；野心勃勃的；宏大的

derivatives.zh: 由 ambitious 还原的名词形式，义为「雄心；抱负；野心」
由 ambitious 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「雄心勃勃地」
由 over- 加 ambitious 构成，义为「野心过大而不切实际的」

senses.title: Strongly desiring success
senses.definition: having a strong desire to achieve success, power, or a high position
senses.definitionCN: 强烈渴望取得成功、权力或高位
senses.example: An ambitious student, she aimed for the top law school.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个有雄心的学生，目标直指顶尖法学院。
senses.why: Ambire in Latin means to go around canvassing votes; the image of someone moving eagerly toward a goal became the desire to rise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambire 意为「四处奔走拉票」；那种朝着目标积极奔走的画面，固化成了「渴望向上爬」的词义。

senses.title: Demanding great effort or resources
senses.titleCN: 规模宏大的；需要巨大投入的
senses.definition: describing a plan or goal that is large in scale and hard to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 形容计划或目标规模宏大、实现难度高
senses.example: The bridge was the most ambitious engineering project of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是那个时代最宏大的工程项目。
senses.why: A person full of desire sets goals larger than ordinary ones; the word then transfers from the desiring person to the oversized goal.
senses.whyCN: 欲望强烈的人定的目标往往超出常规；词义便从「有欲望的人」转移到「超常的目标」上。

senses.title: Eager in a negative, self-seeking way
senses.titleCN: 野心勃勃的；不择手段的（贬义）
senses.definition: having so strong a desire for power or success that honesty or others' interests may be sacrificed
senses.definitionCN: 对权力或成功的渴望强烈到可能牺牲诚信或他人利益
senses.example: His ambitious scheming cost him old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他野心勃勃的算计让他失去了老朋友。
senses.why: Canvassing for votes edges toward manipulation; desire pushed past fairness turns ambition into scheming.
senses.whyCN: 拉票本就带有操纵意味；欲望越过公平的界限，雄心便滑向「钻营算计」的贬义。

intro.en: Ambitious comes from Latin ambire, to go around, the image of Roman candidates canvassing for votes.
intro.cn: ambitious 源于拉丁语 ambire「四处奔走」，其意象正是罗马候选人四处拉票。

items.en: The roots *ambhi- around and *eigh- to move combine in the sense of going about.
items.cn: 词根 *ambhi-（周围）与 *eigh-（移动）组合成「四处走动」之义。

items.en: Latin ambire meant to go around; ambitio meant a canvassing for office.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambire 意为「四处走动」；ambitio 特指谋求官职时的拉票活动。

items.en: Old French ambicion kept the sense of desire for rank.
items.cn: 古法语 ambicion 保留了对位分的渴求之义。

items.en: English ambition first meant eager striving for honor, often with a negative shade.
items.cn: 英语 ambition 最初指对荣誉的急切追逐，常带贬义。

items.en: The adjective ambitious now praises drive as often as it warns against greed, and also describes huge undertakings.
items.cn: 现代形容词 ambitious 既赞许进取心也警示贪欲，还可形容规模浩大的事业。

note.en: Ambitious stands between aspiring and grasping, and pairs with its noun ambition.
note.cn: ambitious 介于褒义的 aspiring 与贬义的 grasping 之间，与其名词 ambition 配套。

entries.definition: the atmosphere of a place
entries.definitionCN: 环境气氛，与 ambitious 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: open to more than one meaning
entries.definitionCN: 歧义的，同用 ambi-（两边）前缀，但词义无关

entries.definition: surrounding on all sides
entries.definitionCN: 周围的、环境的，同用 ambi-（两边）词根，但与「雄心」义完全无关

entries.definition: lacking ambition
entries.definitionCN: 没有雄心的，由 ambition 加 -less 构成

entries.definition: directing one's hopes toward a goal
entries.definitionCN: 有志向的，褒义色彩更浓

entries.definition: showing initiative and willingness to take risks
entries.definitionCN: 有进取心的、敢闯的，强调行动力

entries.definition: relentlessly motivated
entries.definitionCN: 发奋的、有内驱力的

entries.definition: greedy for gain
entries.definitionCN: 贪得无厌的，对应贬义义项

entries.definition: satisfied with what one has
entries.definitionCN: 知足的、安分的，反义对照

normalIntro.en: Link ambitious to ambition and the Latin image of going around.
normalIntro.cn: 把 ambitious 与 ambition 及拉丁语「四处奔走」的画面连起来记。

normal.en: ambitious is simply ambition plus the adjective ending -ous.
normal.cn: ambitious 就是 ambition 加形容词后缀 -ous。

normal.en: Latin ambire, to go around, is behind both words.
normal.cn: 两个词都出自拉丁语 ambire「四处走动」。

normal.en: Roman candidates literally went around asking for votes.
normal.cn: 罗马候选人字面上就是四处奔走求票。

normal.en: overambitious warns that the goal overshot the means.
normal.cn: overambitious 警示目标超出了手段。

normal.en: be ambitious FOR someone means wanting success on their behalf.
normal.cn: be ambitious for someone 表示为某人抱有期望。

abstract.en: See a climber who refuses to check the view because only the summit exists.
abstract.cn: 想象一位登山者无暇看风景，因为眼里只有山顶。

abstract.en: Picture blueprints on a wall that show ten stores instead of one.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上钉着的设计图，不是一家店而是十家店的蓝图。

abstract.en: Feel the hairline between fire in the heart and fire that burns others.
abstract.cn: 感受心中之火与灼伤他人之火之间那条细线。

examples.en: She is ambitious and studies late every night.
examples.cn: 她雄心勃勃，每晚都学习到深夜。

examples.en: Launching the magazine in six months was an ambitious plan.
examples.cn: 六个月内创办杂志是个雄心勃勃的计划。

examples.en: The plot was driven by an ambitious general.
examples.cn: 这场阴谋是由一个野心勃勃的将军推动的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必胜」——俺必定要胜过所有人，胸中燃着这把火的人就是 ambitious：有雄心的，甚至野心勃勃。

root: 拉丁语 ambi-（周围）+ ire（走），ambire 意为「四处奔走」；名词 ambitio 最初指候选人拉票求官，后泛指对功名的追逐。同族词 ambition、ambience。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from personal drive, through oversized undertakings, to ruthless self-seeking.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「个人的上进心」出发，经「规模宏大的事业」，延伸到「不择手段的野心」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: climbing hard because only the summit matters
core.cn: 核心意象：因为只在乎山顶而拼命攀登

branches.en: The inner fire to rise
branches.cn: 渴望上升的内心之火

branches.en: Grand goals born from grand desire
branches.cn: 宏大的欲望孕育宏大的目标

branches.en: Projects that dwarf ordinary plans
branches.cn: 令寻常计划相形见绌的工程

branches.en: Desire crossing from drive into scheming
branches.cn: 欲望从进取滑向钻营

branches.en: Others sacrificed on the way up
branches.cn: 攀登途中被牺牲的他人

intro.en: Ambitious joins ambi- around, the motion of ire, and the adjective ending -ous.
intro.cn: ambitious 由 ambi-（周围）、表移动的 ire 词根和形容词后缀 -ous 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ambire and ambitio carry the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ambire 与 ambitio 支撑起整个词族。

derivatives.zh: 野心过大而不切实际的

definition_zh: 基因组的；与整套遗传物质有关的
definition_en: relating to a genome or to the study of whole sets of genetic material
core_image: 一台机器同时读出成千上万段指令，屏幕上是一整面密密的条带
scene: 一台机器同时读出成千上万段遗传密码。 Genomic data now arrive faster than any single laboratory can interpret.
sceneCN: 这里 genomic 指「与整个基因组有关的」（第 1 个义项：与基因组相关的）；句意为基因组数据到来的速度超过任何单一实验室的解读能力。可辨识物件：测序仪、密集条带屏幕、样本盘、数据线。

pos.zh: 基因组的；全基因组层面的

derivatives.zh: 基因组学研究者（非正式）

senses.title: Relating to a genome
senses.definition: relating to the complete set of genetic material of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 与一个生物体全部遗传物质相关
senses.example: Genomic analysis compared every gene in the two strains.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组分析比较了两个菌株中的每一个基因。
senses.why: The adjective marks the whole-set level, so it is used even when individual genes are mentioned inside the study.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记整套层面，因此即使研究内部提到单个基因，也仍用它来限定整体。

senses.title: Of genomic sequencing
senses.definition: relating to the reading of a complete set of sequences
senses.definitionCN: 与读取整套序列相关
senses.example: Genomic sequencing produced millions of short reads.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组测序产生了数百万条短读段。
senses.why: Sequencing gave the adjective its most common noun: the technique reads the set at once rather than gene by gene.
senses.whyCN: 测序给了这个形容词最常见的搭配：该技术一次读取整套，而非逐个基因读取。

senses.title: Of genomic medicine
senses.definition: relating to medical care guided by whole-genome information
senses.definitionCN: 与由全基因组信息指导的医疗相关
senses.example: Genomic medicine matches drugs to a patient's variants.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组医学把药物与患者的变体相匹配。
senses.why: When the set informs treatment, the adjective moves from research to the clinic without changing its scale.
senses.whyCN: 当整套信息用于治疗，这个形容词从研究走向临床，尺度并未改变。

senses.title: Of genomic data
senses.definition: relating to the large datasets produced by reading genomes
senses.definitionCN: 与读取基因组所产生的大数据集相关
senses.example: Genomic data raise questions of privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组数据引发隐私问题。
senses.why: The data sense is about volume and sensitivity, which is why privacy follows genomic so naturally.
senses.whyCN: 数据义关乎体量与敏感性，因此隐私问题会如此自然地跟随 genomic。

senses.title: Of genomic variation
senses.definition: relating to differences across whole genomes
senses.definitionCN: 与整条基因组之间的差异相关
senses.example: Genomic variation explains why siblings differ.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组变异解释了兄弟姐妹为何不同。
senses.why: The adjective expands variation from one locus to the whole set, so it can explain differences that single genes cannot.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把变异从一个位点扩展到整套，因此能解释单基因无法解释的差异。

senses.title: Of genomic research
senses.definition: relating to research conducted at the scale of whole genomes
senses.definitionCN: 与在全基因组尺度上进行的研究相关
senses.example: Genomic research now spans every branch of biology.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组研究如今遍及生物学的每个分支。
senses.why: Because every organism has a genome, the adjective travels across fields that otherwise share little.
senses.whyCN: 因为每种生物都有基因组，这个形容词能跨越原本共享甚少的领域。

senses.title: At whole-genome scale
senses.definition: carried out across the entire set rather than at single sites
senses.definitionCN: 在整套层面而非单个位点进行
senses.example: The study worked at genomic scale rather than gene by gene.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在全基因组尺度上开展，而非逐个基因进行。
senses.why: Here the adjective names a scale of work, not a kind of object, so it contrasts with single-locus studies.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词命名工作尺度，而非对象种类，因此与单位点研究相对。

senses.title: Of genomic selection
senses.definition: relating to breeding decisions based on whole-genome predictions
senses.definitionCN: 与基于全基因组预测的育种决策相关
senses.example: Genomic selection ranks bulls by predicted breeding value.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组选择按预测育种值给公牛排序。
senses.why: In breeding, the set becomes a prediction tool: many markers are combined into one score.
senses.whyCN: 在育种中，整套信息成为预测工具：许多标记被合并为一个分数。

intro.en: Genomic is genome plus the relational suffix -ic. Genome was coined in German in 1920, and genomic followed as the adjective of whole-genome work.
intro.cn: genomic 是 genome 加关系后缀 -ic 构成。genome 于 1920 年以德语造出，genomic 随后成为全基因组工作的形容词。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-; the root form is a reconstruction, and Latin genus is a cognate rather than the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族；该词根形式是重构，拉丁 genus 是同源词而非来源。

items.en: The -ome of genome was extracted from chromosome and marks a complete set; chromosome joins Greek chroma 'colour' and soma 'body'.
items.cn: genome 中的 -ome 从 chromosome 析出，标记完整集合；chromosome 由希腊 chroma「颜色」与 soma「身体」构成。

items.en: Hans Winkler coined Genom in 1920, usually explained as a blend of Gen 'gene' and Chromosom 'chromosome'.
items.cn: 汉斯·温克勒于 1920 年造出 Genom，通常解释为 Gen「基因」与 Chromosom「染色体」的混成。

items.en: Genomic was formed with -ic to mark relation to a genome; its first recorded use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: genomic 由 -ic 构成，标记与基因组的关系；其最早书证没有精确年代。

items.en: With genomics in the late 1980s, genomic became the standard adjective for data, medicine and selection at whole-genome scale.
items.cn: 随着 20 世纪 80 年代末基因组学的兴起，genomic 成为全基因组尺度的数据、医学与选择的标准形容词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the coinage of genome is documented, but the first use of genomic is approximate, and no Latin derivative exists, so latinEntries is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：genome 的造词有文献可查，但 genomic 的最早使用只是约数；不存在拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

note.en: Group one separates genomic from same-root adjectives and one accidental sound-alike; group two separates it from genetic and from the neighbouring whole-set sciences.
note.cn: 第一组把 genomic 与同根形容词及一个偶然音近词分开；第二组把它与 genetic 及相邻的整套学科词区分。

entries.definition: Relating to genes, often one or a few at a time; genomic refers to the whole set.
entries.definitionCN: 与基因相关，常指一个或少数几个；genomic 指整套。

entries.definition: The study of genomes; genomic is the adjective, genomics the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究基因组的学科；genomic 是形容词，genomics 是学科。

entries.definition: At the level of the genome; the adverb marks the respect in which a claim holds.
entries.definitionCN: 在基因组层面；副词标记断言成立的方面。

entries.definition: From Greek gnome 'maxim, thought', not genos: expressed in short, obscure maxims. The resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 gnome「格言、思想」，并非 genos：指以简短隐晦的格言表达。相似仅在读音。

entries.definition: Gene-level in focus; genomic is whole-set in focus, though both belong to the same field.
entries.definitionCN: 聚焦基因层面；genomic 聚焦整套，但两者属于同一领域。

entries.definition: The discipline that produces genomic data; the adjective names what belongs to that scale.
entries.definitionCN: 产生基因组数据的学科；形容词命名属于该尺度的事物。

entries.definition: Relating to all transcripts rather than all genes; the suffix is shared but the object differs.
entries.definitionCN: 与全部转录本相关而非全部基因；后缀相同但对象不同。

entries.definition: Relating to the complete set of proteins, downstream of the genome.
entries.definitionCN: 与全部蛋白质相关，位于基因组下游。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genome + -ic: belonging to the whole set.
normal.cn: genome + -ic：属于整套。

normal.en: The family runs genome, genomic, genomics and genomically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 genome、genomic、genomics 与 genomically。

normal.en: Genomic data, genomic medicine and genomic selection are fixed phrases.
normal.cn: 基因组数据、基因组医学与基因组选择是固定搭配。

normal.en: Genomic is whole-set; genetic is gene-level.
normal.cn: genomic 是整套层面；genetic 是基因层面。

normal.en: Genomics is the field; genomic is its adjective.
normal.cn: genomics 是领域；genomic 是它的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture an entire shelf read at once instead of one book at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象整排书架一次被读完，而不是一次读一本。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every street is visible at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一张所有街道同时可见的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a weather report that covers a continent, not one town.
abstract.cn: 想象一份覆盖整块大陆而非一个小镇的气象报告。

examples.en: Genomic sequencing has become cheaper than many single-gene tests.
examples.cn: 基因组测序已比许多单基因检测更便宜。

examples.en: The clinic opened a genomic medicine service last year.
examples.cn: 这家诊所去年开设了基因组医学服务。

examples.en: Genomic selection shortened the breeding cycle by half.
examples.cn: 基因组选择把育种周期缩短了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: genome（基因组）+ ic（形容词尾）——整个基因组的 → 基因组的；与 genetic（基因层面的）相对。

root: genome + -ic；genome 来自德语 Genom（温克勒，1920）＝Gen「基因」+ Chromosom「染色体」混成；gen 源于希腊 genos「种族、种类」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one scale: the whole genome, its sequencing, its medical use, its data, its variation, its research, its scale and its use in breeding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个尺度展开：整个基因组、其测序、其医学用途、其数据、其变异、其研究、其尺度与育种用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a machine reading thousands of instruction strips at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台机器同时读取成千上万段指令条。

branches.en: WHOLE-SET SCALE: the adjective always marks the set, whether as object or as scale of work.
branches.cn: 整套尺度：这个形容词始终标记整套，无论作为对象还是工作尺度。

branches.en: READING AND DATA: sequencing produces the reads, and the reads become sensitive data.
branches.cn: 读取与数据：测序产生读段，读段成为敏感数据。

branches.en: MEDICINE: whole-genome information guides treatment.
branches.cn: 医学：全基因组信息指导治疗。

branches.en: VARIATION AND RESEARCH: differences across sets, and a field that spans biology.
branches.cn: 变异与研究：整套之间的差异，以及横跨生物学的领域。

branches.en: BREEDING: many markers combined into one predicted score.
branches.cn: 育种：许多标记合并为一个预测分数。

intro.en: Genomic is genome plus a relation suffix; the stem goes back through German to Greek, and the suffix family names the whole-set sciences.
intro.cn: genomic 是 genome 加关系后缀；词干经德语上溯希腊，后缀家族命名整套层面的各门学科。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos gives gene; -ome from chromosome gives genome; -ic gives genomic, and -ics gives genomics. No Latin derivative exists, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos 衍生 gene；来自 chromosome 的 -ome 构成 genome；-ic 构成 genomic，-ics 构成 genomics。不存在拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: The stem names a reproducing kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名自我繁衍的类。

items.example: The suffix marks a whole collection.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记完整集合。

items.example: The suffix forms a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。
基因组学比较完整序列。
样本在基因组层面做了比较。

items.example: A gene is a unit of heredity.

definition_zh: 分集的；片段式的；间歇发作的
definition_en: arranged or occurring as separate self-contained episodes rather than one continuous whole
core_image: 一本没有装订线的书，每一章单独成页，翻过一页前一页就合上
scene: 评论人称该剧结构松散。 Critics called its structure episodic.
sceneCN: 这里 episodic 是「片段式的」（第 1 个义项：由各自独立的场景拼成）；句意：评论人称该剧结构是片段式的。

pos.zh: 分集的；片段式的；间歇发作的

senses.title: Built out of separate instalments
senses.definition: composed of episodes that each close before the next begins
senses.definitionCN: 由各自收尾的若干片段组合而成
senses.example: The novel is episodic rather than plotted.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是片段式的而非情节连贯的。
senses.why: Each instalment keeps its own edges, so the shape of the whole reads as a string of beads.
senses.whyCN: 每段自留边界，整体轮廓便读作一串珠子。

senses.title: Memory for personal scenes
senses.definition: relating to the recall of specific events placed in time and place
senses.definitionCN: 指对特定时空之下具体事件的回忆
senses.example: Patients lose episodic memory first.
senses.exampleCN: 患者最先丧失情景记忆。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word because such memories arrive as scenes, not as facts.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用了这个词，因为这类记忆以场景而非事实到来。

senses.title: Coming in attacks
senses.definition: occurring in distinct bursts with quiet intervals between
senses.definitionCN: 一阵一阵地发作，间歇期平静
senses.example: Doctors described an episodic fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生描述了一种间歇性发热。
senses.why: Medicine took the narrative sense over, since a bout is a story with an end.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了叙事义，因为一次病发本就是一段有结尾的故事。

intro.en: Episodic hangs from episode, Greek epeisodion, the interlude between two choruses.
intro.cn: episodic 挂在 episode 之下，源头是希腊语 epeisodion，指两次合唱之间的插段。

items.en: Hodos names a road or way.
items.cn: hodos 指道路。

items.en: Epeisodion marks an episode inserted between choral songs.
items.cn: epeisodion 指合唱之间插入的一段。

items.en: Episode transcribes the Greek noun.
items.cn: 拉丁语 episode 转写希腊名词。

items.en: Episode enters English by way of French.
items.cn: episode 经法语进入英语。

items.en: Literary critics attach the adjectival ending.
items.cn: 十九世纪文学批评加上了形容词词尾。

items.en: Television and psychology both adopt the adjective.
items.cn: 二十世纪的电视业与心理学同时采用了该形容词。

note.en: Group one holds relatives of the Greek way and instalment; group two holds other adjectives of broken sequence.
note.cn: 第一组是希腊语「道路」与「插段」的亲族；第二组是其他表断续的形容词。

entries.definition: One instalment, or an incident set apart from routine.
entries.definitionCN: 一集，或从日常中划出的一件事。

entries.definition: Returning at intervals, closer to rhythm than to narrative.
entries.definitionCN: 按间隔复现，偏向节奏而非叙事。

entries.definition: Built on the same Greek word for a road, meaning orderly.
entries.definitionCN: 同出希腊语道路一词，意为有条理。

entries.definition: Made of brief unpublished stories, loosely like episodic.
entries.definitionCN: 由未刊小段故事组成，与片段式略近。

entries.definition: Consisting of incomplete parts rather than closed scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 由不完整部分构成，而非闭合场景。

entries.definition: Lacking transitions between one part and the next.
entries.definitionCN: 部分之间缺少过渡。

entries.definition: Pausing and resuming, used chiefly of processes.
entries.definitionCN: 停停续续，多修饰过程。

entries.definition: Published in successive parts, often still one story.
entries.definitionCN: 分期刊载，仍常为同一故事。

normalIntro.en: Episodic stresses that the parts stand alone; serial stresses that they follow one another.
normalIntro.cn: episodic 强调各段独立，serial 强调前后相续。

normal.en: It is neutral in criticism but often implies weak overall plot.
normal.cn: 在批评中语气中性，但常暗示整体情节薄弱。

normal.en: Episodic memory is a fixed term in psychology.
normal.cn: episodic memory 是心理学固定术语。

normal.en: Pair with structure, format, pattern, series.
normal.cn: 搭配 structure、format、pattern、series。

normal.en: In medicine it means attacks with clear gaps.
normal.cn: 医学上指发作之间有明显空隙。

normal.en: Avoid it for a story that merely has chapters.
normal.cn: 仅有章节的故事不必用这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a necklace of separate glass beads.
abstract.cn: 想象一串彼此独立的玻璃珠。

abstract.en: Imagine a television series you can start at any episode.
abstract.cn: 想象一部从任意一集都能入戏的电视剧。

abstract.en: Think of a fever that lights and goes out like a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想想一盏点亮又熄灭的灯那样的一阵发热。

examples.en: Her early career was episodic, three months here, four there.
examples.cn: 她的早期生涯断断续续，这儿三个月，那儿四个月。

examples.en: Episodic delivery lets writers restart without recap.
examples.cn: 分集播出让编剧无需前情回顾即可重启。

examples.en: The diary stays episodic, one weather entry per day.
examples.cn: 这本日记保持片段式，每天一条天气记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: “爱批散”——爱把整块材料批成散段，一段自成一体，所以 episodic 是分集的、片段式的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在……之上）＋ hodos（路）→ epeisodion（合唱之间插入的一段）→ episode ＋ 词尾 -ic → episodic，核心义「一段一段自成起讫」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective describes narrative shape, a memory system, and a pattern of attacks.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词描述叙事形态、一种记忆系统，以及发作的节律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: closed scenes set side by side with visible gaps between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：各自闭合的场景并列摆放，中间留有可见的空隙。

branches.en: Storytelling hands each scene its own door.
branches.cn: 叙事为每一场戏留一扇门。

branches.en: Memory files the day by scene rather than by rule.
branches.cn: 记忆按场景而非按规则归档。

branches.en: The body opens and closes its attacks like chapters.
branches.cn: 身体像翻章一样开启并结束发作。

branches.en: Both divide experience into packaged units.
branches.cn: 两者都把体验打包成单元。

branches.en: Both depend on recall of when a thing happened.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖对何时发生的回忆。

intro.en: A prefix of position, a noun of road, and an adjectival ending stack in order.
intro.cn: 表位置的前缀、表道路的名词与形容词词尾依次叠起。

latinIntro.en: Greek hodos is a way, epeisodion an interlude, periodos a circuit.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 hodos 表道路，epeisodion 表插段，periodos 表环绕。

items.example: A cousin built on the same hodos.
items.exampleCN: 同一 hodos 上的表亲词。
meta- 加 hodos 构成 method。
